questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city passed an ordinance requiring individuals to obtain a license in order to care for children under the age of 12 for pay. City officials who promoted the ordinance said that the licensing process would ensure that child-care workers were adequately regulated for the health and safety of the city's children. To receive a license, the ordinance requires an individual to complete 10 hours of instruction in child care, undergo a background check, and pay a $100 fee. The ordinance affects women disproportionately to men, because female child-care workers far outnumber male child-care workers in the city.
Is the ordinance constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it has a disparate impact on women without a showing that the ordinance is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.
choices.B: No, because it infringes on the freedom of contract without a compelling government interest.
choices.C: Yes, because any burden it imposes is clearly outweighed by an important government objective.
choices.D: Yes, because it is rationally related to a legitimate government objective.

questions.explanation:
Intentional discrimination

Facial discrimination

S.789
One Hundred Sixteenth Congress
of the
United States of America
AT THE FIRST SESSION
An Act
Sec. Two
Males shall be
preferred for
government
employment.

Discriminatory application

STATE DMV
All applicants welcome!
Only consider men.

Discriminatory impact

CITY COUNCIL
This will keep most women out.
Discriminatory laws challenged under the equal protection clause are generally subject to rational basis scrutiny, which requires that a law be rationally related to a legitimate government objective. But heightened scrutiny is used when a law (1) substantially impacts a fundamental right or (2) intentionally discriminates against a suspect or quasi-suspect class. Intentional discrimination can be seen on a law's:
  • face – the language of the law distinguishes between different classes (intent presumed)
  • application – a facially neutral law is purposefully applied differently to different classes or
  • motive – an otherwise neutral law was enacted to disproportionately impact a protected class.
Here, although the ordinance disproportionately affects women (quasi-suspect class), it is not subject to heightened scrutiny since there is no evidence that this discrimination was intentional. That is because the ordinance:
  • requires that all child-care workers obtain a license (no facial discrimination)
  • is applied equally to men and women (no discriminatory application) and
  • was not enacted to target women (no discriminatory motive).
And since the ordinance is rationally related to the government's legitimate interest in the health and safety of children, it is constitutional.

(Choice A) The city would have had to prove that the ordinance was necessary to serve a compelling government interest (ie, strict scrutiny) had it substantially impacted a fundamental right or intentionally discriminated against a suspect class. Since the ordinance does neither, it need only survive rational basis review.

(Choice B) The freedom of contract is protected by the contracts clause, which restricts state and local legislatures from impairing existing contracts. Since the ordinance affects the ability to enter into future contracts for child-care services, it does not violate this clause.

(Choice C) Had the ordinance intentionally discriminated against women, the city would have had to prove that the ordinance is substantially related to an important government objective (ie, intermediate scrutiny)– not that this objective clearly outweighs any burden the ordinance imposes.

📌 Educational Objective

Heightened equal protection review is appropriate when a law intentionally discriminates—on its face, in its application, or in its motive—against a quasi-suspect or suspect class.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).
  • Pers. Adm'r of Mass. v. Feeney, 442 U.S. 256, 274 (1979) (explaining that a neutral law's disparate impact on a quasi-suspect or suspect class, standing alone, is insufficient to require heightened scrutiny).
questions.zh-question:
某市通过一项法令，要求为12岁以下儿童提供有偿看护服务的个人必须获得执照。推动该法令的市政官员表示，执照审批程序将确保托儿工作者受到充分监管，以保障本市儿童的健康与安全。根据该法令，要获得执照，个人必须完成10小时的托儿指导课程，接受背景调查，并支付100美元的费用。该法令对女性的影响不成比例地大于男性，因为在该市，女性托儿工作者的数量远超男性。

该法令是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为它对女性产生了不成比例的影响，且未能证明该法令对于服务于一项迫切的政府利益是必要的。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为它在没有迫切政府利益的情况下，侵犯了合同自由。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为它所施加的任何负担显然被一项重要的政府目标所超越。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为它与一项合法的政府目标具有理性关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - General Considerations

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：一个表面中立、但对女性影响更大的儿童照护许可条例，是否因为差别影响（disparate impact）就要按更严格的平等保护审查；答案是先看有没有故意歧视（intentional discrimination），没有就回到理性基础审查（rational basis review）。

三秒认题路径：

表面中立 → 女性受影响大 → 先看故意 → 没有故意 → 理性基础

核心法律规则

平等保护条款（equal protection clause）下，普通规则是用理性基础审查（rational basis review）：政府只要能说清楚这条规定和一个合法政府目标（legitimate government objective）有合理关系，就能过关。

只有当法律在表面（face）、适用方式（application）或制定动机（motive）上，故意针对嫌疑或准嫌疑群体（suspect/quasi-suspect class）时，才会拉高审查等级。

这里虽然女性受影响更多，但题干没有任何证据显示它是故意针对女性，所以还是按rational basis走，不会上升到中间审查（intermediate scrutiny）或严格审查（strict scrutiny）。

核心判例： Pers. Adm'r of Mass. v. Feeney — 只有差别影响不够；要把审查拉高，得有故意歧视。

思维导图

题干：儿童照护许可条例，女性受影响更多，但看不出故意针对女性
先问有没有故意歧视（intentional discrimination）？
没有只有差别影响，不够把审查抬高
再回到理性基础审查（rational basis review）
看目标儿童健康与安全
看结果要求培训、背景审查、收费，和目标有合理关系
结论合宪，选 D

考点陷阱

你可能会想：women outnumber men，所以这条规定一定要按更高审查来打。

但考试真正问的是：有没有证据证明政府是故意针对女性，不是单纯看结果偏向谁。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里也是一样，看的是有没有故意歧视，不是只盯着差别影响的数字。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干只有女性受影响更大这一点，没有facial / application / motive层面的故意歧视；因此只用理性基础审查（rational basis review），而市政府的儿童健康与安全目标足够了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 审查等级误判

✕ A: 把disparate impact直接当成故意歧视，硬上严格审查了。

❌ 法律适用 | 合同条款误搬

✕ B: 乱搬freedom of contract，这题问的是平等保护，不是现有合同被没收。

❌ 事实误判 | 把影响当目的

✕ C: 看到女性受影响多就套important government objective，但题干没故意歧视。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有没有故意歧视”，再决定审查等级；只有差别影响时别急着升档。

考场速记

记住一句：差别影响（disparate impact）不等于故意歧视（intentional discrimination）；没有故意，通常还是rational basis。下一次看到“很多女性被影响”，先问“题干有没有写政府故意这么干”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state law imposes penalties for "any public statement containing false or misleading information about a service or product." An airline falsely claimed in an advertisement that its competitor had an inferior safety record. The claim was based on erroneous information, found on the website of a nonprofit consumer advocacy group, that the airline assumed to be true. The airline was charged under the state law for making a false statement. No federal statute applies.
Which of the following best supports the airline in a defense based on the First Amendment?

choices.A: Its statement about the safety record was made without malice.
choices.B: Its statement about the safety record was protected noncommercial speech.
choices.C: The state law is a prior restraint.
choices.D: The state law is overbroad.

questions.explanation:
Constitutional challenges
Facial
  • No application of law would be constitutional
  • Strike down law in its entirety
As applied
  • Generally valid law is unconstitutional as to challenger
  • Overturn application of law against challenger

The state law cannot be challenged as applied to the airline's false advertisement because the First Amendment does not protect commercial speech that is (1) false or misleading or (2) concerns an unlawful activity. But the airline can still use the First Amendment to challenge the law on its face based on the overbreadth doctrine. Under this doctrine, a law is unenforceable against anyone—including those engaged in unprotected speech—if it restricts a substantial amount of constitutionally protected speech.

Here, the law penalizes "any public statement containing false or misleading information about a service or product." And though this encompasses unprotected commercial speech, it also impacts a substantial amount of protected speech—eg, false or misleading noncommercial speech. Therefore, the airline's best defense is that the law is overbroad.

(Choice A) Defamation of a public official or figure (eg, the airline's competitor) requires proof that the speaker acted with malice—ie, knowingly or recklessly disregarded the falsity of its published statement. And though the airline's lack of malice may show that its advertisement was not defamatory, the false advertisement is still unprotected speech. Therefore, this evidence would not aid the airline's defense.

(Choice B) The airline's claim about the competitor's safety record was commercial speech because it was used in an advertisement—a type of economically-oriented expression. And it was unprotected commercial speech because it contained false information.

(Choice C) A prior restraint is a government action (eg, an injunction) that prohibits speech before it occurs. But the state law is not a prior restraint since it imposes penalties after speech occurs.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the overbreadth doctrine, a law is unenforceable against anyone—including those engaged in unprotected speech—if it restricts a substantial amount of constitutionally protected speech.

📚 References
  • Houston v. Hill, 482 U.S. 451, 458–59 (1987) (explaining the overbreadth doctrine).
questions.zh-question:
某州法律规定，对“任何包含关于服务或产品的虚假或误导性信息的公开声明”处以刑罚。一家航空公司在一则广告中谎称其竞争对手的安全记录较差。该主张基于一家非营利性消费者权益保护组织网站上的错误信息，而该航空公司想当然地认为该信息是真实的。该航空公司因发表虚假声明而根据州法律被起诉。没有适用的联邦法规。

以下哪一项最能支持该航空公司基于第一修正案的辩护？

zh-choices.A: 其关于安全记录的声明是在没有恶意的情况下作出的。
zh-choices.B: 其关于安全记录的声明是受保护的非商业言论。
zh-choices.C: 该州法律是一种事先限制。
zh-choices.D: 该州法律过于宽泛。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation of speech

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州法把“任何关于商品或服务的虚假或误导性陈述”一概罚掉时，能不能用 过度广泛原则（overbreadth doctrine） 从表面上直接打掉，而不是只争自己这一次广告。

三秒认题路径：

广告罚言论 → 先看是否商业言论 → 不能只看本案 → 查 表面挑战（facial challenge）

核心法律规则

表面挑战（facial challenge） 的意思是：不是只说“这次罚我不对”，而是说这条法本身有问题，连它对别人也会压到受保护言论，所以整条法都站不住。过度广泛原则（overbreadth doctrine） 的考场意思：即使这次原告自己的言论不受保护，只要该法顺带扫到“大量”受宪法保护的言论，也可以直接挑战整部法。

这题里，州法罚的是“任何”虚假或误导性公共陈述，范围不只罩住 商业言论（commercial speech），也会碰到不少受保护的非商业虚假陈述，所以本题不是问“这次广告能不能被罚”，而是问“这条法会不会把太多可保护的言论一起拖下水”。

核心判例： Houston v. Hill —— 说明一条法如果会压到大量受保护言论，就可能因过度广泛而失效。

思维导图

先问：能不能只按这次广告做 as applied 挑战？
先卡住：这次是广告里的虚假安全记录，属于 商业言论（commercial speech），而且是虚假内容，这条路通常救不了 airline。
再问：能不能改走 表面挑战（facial challenge）？
关键关卡：这部法写成“任何虚假或误导性公共陈述” → 不只打到没保护的商业广告，也会打到受保护的非商业言论。
第三要件：如果它限制了“大量”受宪法保护的言论，整条法可因 overbreadth 被打掉。
结论：不是靠“我这次没恶意”翻盘，而是靠“这条法扫太宽”拿下 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然航空公司是拿错资料、也没有恶意，那就应该直接赢。

但考试真正问的是：这条州法会不会把太多本来受保护的言论也一起罚掉，所以争点是“法太宽”，不是“这次广告有没有坏心”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 any public statement 这种写法会把受保护的非商业言论也一起罩住，所以航空公司可以抓住 过度广泛原则（overbreadth doctrine） 直接打州法。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 你把 malice 当成本题胜负点了，它只管诽谤，不管这条法是否扫太宽。

❌ 事实误判 | 语境偷换误判

✕ B: 你只盯着广告是 commercial speech，却漏了本题要打的是州法本身。

❌ 法律适用 | 先后顺序误判

✕ C: 这不是事前禁言的 prior restraint，而是事后处罚，所以别把概念搬错。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“这次能不能罚”还是“这条法能不能活”，再看是否碰到 overbreadth。

考场速记

记住：过度广泛原则（overbreadth doctrine） 盯的是“法会不会顺手伤到很多受保护言论”，不是只盯原告这一次有没有说错。

本题速记：先排 as applied，再看 facial challenge；一旦法文写成“any”，就要立刻想它是不是扫太宽。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The legislature of State B enacted a statute requiring that all law enforcement officers in that state be United States citizens. A lawfully admitted noncitizen became a permanent resident five years before the enactment of this statute. He sought employment as a forensic pathologist in the state coroner's office. He was denied that job solely because he was not a citizen. The resident noncitizen thereupon brought suit in federal district court against appropriate state officials seeking to invalidate this citizenship requirement on federal constitutional grounds.
Which of the following is the strongest ground upon which to attack this citizenship requirement?

choices.A: The requirement constitutes an ex post facto law as to previously admitted noncitizens.
choices.B: The requirement denies noncitizens equal protection of the laws guaranteed by the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.C: The requirement denies noncitizens the right to employment in violation of the privileges or immunities clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.D: The requirement deprives noncitizens of a fundamental right to employment without the due process of law under the Fourteenth Amendment.

questions.explanation:
Fourteenth Amendment protections
Clause Applicability
Equal protection Discriminatory treatment of similarly situated people
Due process Substantive – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate justification
Procedural – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate process
Privileges or
immunities*		 Interference with rights of national citizenship
*Rarely a correct answer.

Citizenship requirements (as seen here) are discriminatory since they deny resident noncitizens benefits or opportunities that are generally available to U.S. citizens. As a result, laws with this requirement can be attacked on equal protection grounds. And since citizenship is a suspect class (triggering strict scrutiny review), these laws are rarely upheld.

(Choice A) An ex post facto law typically refers to a criminal statute that retroactively imposes punishment. Although federal and state governments are barred from passing such laws, State B's statute is civil (not criminal) in nature and has no retroactive effect—ie, there is no requirement that noncitizens currently holding law enforcement positions be terminated.

(Choice C) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause only protects citizens (not noncitizens or corporations) from unreasonable state interference with the narrowly defined rights of national citizenship.

(Choice D) A state law that impacts a fundamental right can be challenged on Fourteenth Amendment due process (or equal protection) grounds. But since employment is not a fundamental right, State B's citizenship requirement cannot be attacked on this basis.

📌 Educational Objective

Citizenship requirements are discriminatory since they deny resident noncitizens benefits or opportunities that are generally available to citizens. As a result, they are strictly scrutinized (and rarely upheld) on equal protection grounds.

📚 References
  • Cabell v. Chavez-Salido, 454 U.S. 432, 437 (1982) (explaining that a resident noncitizen can challenge citizenship requirement for public employment).
questions.zh-question: B州立法机关颁布了一项法规，要求该州所有执法人员必须是美国公民。一名合法入境的非公民在该法规颁布前五年成为永久居民。他寻求在州验尸官办公室担任法医病理学家。他仅因非公民身份而被拒绝该职位。该居民非公民随后在联邦地区法院对相关州官员提起诉讼，寻求以联邦宪法为由宣告该公民身份要求无效。以下哪项是攻击该公民身份要求的最有力的理由？

zh-choices.A: 该要求对先前入境的非公民构成了追溯性法律 (ex post facto law)。
zh-choices.B: 该要求剥夺了非公民受第十四修正案保障的法律的平等保护 (equal protection of the laws)。
zh-choices.C: 该要求违反了第十四修正案的特权或豁免条款 (privileges or immunities clause)，剥夺了非公民的就业权。
zh-choices.D: 该要求在没有第十四修正案规定的正当法律程序 (due process of law) 的情况下，剥夺了非公民的基本就业权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Suspect classifications

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府把公职门槛设成“必须是美国公民”，是否属于对非公民的歧视性分类，所以要走 平等保护（equal protection） 这条线。

三秒认题路径：

公民门槛 → 非公民被拒 → 歧视分类 → 平等保护 → 严格审查

核心法律规则

非公民（noncitizens） 受州法歧视时，考试先看是不是在用“公民身份”把一群人挡在普通公职外。公民身份分类（alienage classification） 的考场意思：这通常会被当成可疑分类，直接上 严格审查（strict scrutiny）。

如果这类法律只是把“非公民”排除在一般公共职位之外，通常会被判得很严，因为它是在剥夺本来对居民开放的机会。这里最稳的攻击点不是 due process（正当程序），而是 equal protection（平等保护）。

核心判例： Cabell v. Chavez-Salido — 住民非公民可以用平等保护去挑战州里的公职公民资格要求。

思维导图

州法要求“必须是美国公民”才能做这份州公职？
是：这是对 非公民（noncitizens） 的分类。
默认路径：平等保护（equal protection） + 严格审查（strict scrutiny）。
卡死点：不是“能不能马上上诉”，而是“州能不能拿出足够强的理由”；本题里通常过不了。
别跑偏： ex post facto 只管刑法追溯处罚；privileges or immunities 也不是这里最强武器。
结论：选 B，因为这就是对非公民的歧视分类。
否：就按别的条款或别的考点走。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然它影响的是“工作资格”，那是不是去找 due process（正当程序） 或者说这是剥夺 fundamental right？

但考试真正问的是：州是不是在用“公民身份”把非公民排除在一般公职之外，这种做法首先打 equal protection（平等保护）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同理：不是看这份工作有多重要，而是看分类本身是不是歧视非公民。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 citizenship requirement 直接把住民非公民挡在州公职外，最强攻击点就是 平等保护（equal protection），而且要按可疑分类来审。

❌ 法律适用 | 追溯刑罚误判

✕ A: 把 ex post facto 搬来，但这不是刑事追罚，也没有追溯惩罚。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权条款误判

✕ C: 以为 privileges or immunities 专门管这里，其实它不是非公民挑战州公职门槛的主力。

❌ 事实误判 | 基本权利偷换

✕ D: 把 fundamental right 当成就业权，但“当一份公职”不是这里的基本权利。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“公民身份分类”，再直接套平等保护的严格审查，别被程序、追溯和特权条款带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：公民资格门槛（citizenship requirement） 先想到 equal protection，再想到 strict scrutiny。这类题的口诀就是：resident noncitizen 被排除，先看平等保护，不先找别的条款。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
The United States government demonstrated that terrorist attacks involving commercial airliners were perpetrated exclusively by individuals of one particular race. In response, Congress enacted a statute imposing stringent new airport and airline security measures only on individuals of that race seeking to board airplanes in the United States.
Which of the following provides the best ground for challenging the constitutionality of this statute?

choices.A: The commerce clause of Article I, Section 8.
choices.B: The due process clause of the Fifth Amendment.
choices.C: The privileges and immunities clause of Article IV.
choices.D: The privileges or immunities clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.

questions.explanation:
Fifth Amendment due process challenge
(equal protection principles)
• Rational basis scrutiny •
Constitutional unless
  • not rationally related to
  • legitimate interest
• Intermediate scrutiny •
Unconstitutional unless
  • substantially related to
  • important interest
• Strict scrutiny •
Unconstitutional unless
  • necessary to achieve
  • compelling interest

A law that treats similarly situated persons differently may violate the constitutional principle of equal protection, which applies to the federal government through the Fifth Amendment due process clause.

This is especially likely when the law intentionally discriminates against a suspect class (eg, race). That is because the government must clear the highest hurdle—strict scrutiny—to justify such a law. And since this federal statute intentionally targets a particular race, due process provides the best ground to challenge the statute.

*The equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment applies only to states and localities—not the federal government.

(Choice A) The commerce clause grants Congress broad plenary power to regulate the instrumentalities of interstate commerce—eg, planes, trains, automobiles. Therefore, this clause supports Congress's authority to regulate airports and airlines.

(Choice C) The Article IV privileges and immunities clause generally prohibits states from discriminating against citizens of other states. But it does not apply to the federal government.

(Choice D) The Fourteenth Amendment privileges or immunities clause applies to states—not the federal government—and bars them from depriving individuals of the very limited rights of national citizenship.

📌 Educational Objective

Equal protection principles apply to the federal government through the Fifth Amendment due process clause. And under this clause, federal laws that intentionally discriminate against a suspect class (eg, race) are almost always invalidated under strict scrutiny.

📚 References
  • Bolling v. Sharpe, 347 U.S. 497, 499–500 (1954) (holding that equal protection principles apply to the federal government through the Fifth Amendment due process clause).
questions.zh-question:
美国政府证明，涉及商用客机的恐怖袭击完全是由某一特定种族的个人所为。作为回应，国会颁布了一项法规，仅对在美国寻求登机的该种族个人实施严格的新机场和航空公司安保措施。

以下哪一项为挑战该法规的合宪性提供了最佳依据？

zh-choices.A: Article I, Section 8 的商业条款。
zh-choices.B: Fifth Amendment 的正当程序条款。
zh-choices.C: Article IV 的特权与豁免条款。
zh-choices.D: Fourteenth Amendment 的特权或豁免条款。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Procedural Due Process Applied

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：联邦法如果故意按种族区别对待人，应该用第五修正案正当程序中的平等保护原则来打，而不是去找第十四修正案。

三秒认题路径：

联邦立法 → 按种族区分 → 第五修正案 → 严格审查 → 通常违宪

核心法律规则

平等保护原则（equal protection）不仅管州和地方，也会通过第五修正案正当程序（Fifth Amendment due process）约束联邦政府，所以联邦法不能随便按种族挑人区别对待。

这里牵涉到可疑分类（suspect class）中的种族，考试意思：政府要拿出最强理由，走严格审查（strict scrutiny），否则这条法很容易被打掉。

核心判例：Bolling v. Sharpe - 确认联邦政府也要受平等保护原则约束，抓住本题就是第五修正案。

思维导图

先看是谁在立法？
联邦政府就不能只盯第十四修正案。
这条法是不是按种族筛人？
是。→ 进入平等保护分析
适用哪条宪法入口？
联邦政府的平等保护问题，走第五修正案正当程序。
审查强度是什么？
种族分类 → 严格审查；除非必要实现迫切利益，否则违宪。
所以答案？
选 B：第五修正案正当程序。
如果是第十四修正案？
那是管州，不管联邦；这题故意拿错入口骗你。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然题干讲的是航空安全、国会立法，那就先去找国会权力来源。

但考试真正问的是：这条法能不能按种族把人分开对待，关键是平等保护入口，不是国会有没有权管飞机。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 按种族只限制该人群登机，这是联邦政府的平等保护问题，正确入口是第五修正案正当程序。

❌ 法律适用 | 立法权限误判

✕ A: 把 commerce clause 当成挑战点，但它是在帮国会授权，不是在打掉种族歧视。

❌ 概念混淆 | 州联邦搞混

✕ C: 以为能拿 Article IV 去卡联邦政府，其实它主要管州对外州公民的歧视。

❌ 事实误判 | 修正案对象偷换

✕ D: 把 Privileges or Immunities 甩到联邦头上，但它不是这题的联邦审查入口。

这题建议用什么方法？

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state statute provided state monetary grants to private dance, theater, and opera groups located in that state. The statute required recipients of such grants to use the granted monies for the acquisition, construction, and maintenance of appropriate facilities for the public performance of their performing arts. The last section of the statute conditioned the award of each such grant on the recipient's agreement to refrain from all kinds of political lobbying calculated to secure additional tax support for the performing arts.
Which of the following provides the strongest constitutional basis to attack the validity of the last section of the statute?

choices.A: Commerce clause.
choices.B: Fifth Amendment.
choices.C: First and Fourteenth Amendments.
choices.D: Obligation of contracts clause.

questions.explanation:
Explanation

Conditions on government funding
Funded
activities		 Government can restrict use of funds to authorized purposes "Grant monies must be used for the acquisition, construction, and maintenance of appropriate performance facilities"
Funding
recipients		 Government cannot restrict protected conduct unrelated to funding's purpose "Recipient must agree to refrain from all kinds of political lobbying calculated to secure additional tax support for the performing arts"

The last section of the statute conditions state funding on a recipient's agreement to refrain from certain political lobbying efforts. Since this condition interferes with the First Amendment right to free expression—which is applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment—the section can be challenged on that basis. But due to the government's countervailing right to decide how to spend its funds, the success of this attack depends on whether the condition is placed on:

  • funded activities – in which case, the government can insist that the funds be used for authorized purposes or
  • funding recipients – in which case, the government cannot restrict the recipient's right to engage in protected conduct that falls outside the funding's purpose or scope (as seen here).

Political lobbying is protected First Amendment conduct that is unrelated to the activities—acquiring, constructing, and maintaining performing arts facilities—that are funded by the statute. And since the statute conditions the award of such grants on the recipient's agreement to refrain from such conduct, the First and Fourteenth Amendments provide the strongest constitutional basis to attack this section of the statute.

(Choice A) The commerce clause bars states from discriminating against interstate commerce by favoring in-state over out-of-state economic interests unless the state acts as a market participant (eg, by providing grants—as seen here). Therefore, this is a weak basis to attack the last section's constitutionality.

(Choice B) The Fifth Amendment does not, by itself, provide a basis to attack the last section since the Fifth Amendment only applies to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment.

📌 Educational Objective

The government can condition funding on the promise that the funds be used for a particular purpose. But it cannot condition funding on a recipient's promise to refrain from engaging in protected First Amendment conduct if that conduct is unrelated to the funding's purpose or scope.

📚 References
  • Agency for Int'l Dev. v. All. for Open Soc'y Int'l, Inc., 570 U.S. 205, 221 (2013) (holding that a state funding program violated the First Amendment by conditioning funds on requirements unrelated to the program's purpose).
  • Rust v. Sullivan, 500 U.S. 173, 192–200 (1991) (upholding a federal funding program that limited fund recipients' ability to provide abortion-related services that were outside the program's scope).

以下哪项为质疑该法最后一节的有效性提供了最有力的宪法依据？

zh-choices.A: 商业条款。
zh-choices.B: 第五修正案。
zh-choices.C: 第一和第十四修正案。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Miscellaneous

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府给钱时，能不能把受款人对受补助者（recipient）的条件，变成放弃第一修正案（First Amendment）保护的政治游说。

三秒认题路径：

政府发钱 → 条件附加 → 游说受限 → 不是项目内用途 → 看第一和第十四修正案

核心法律规则

政府可以把补助金限定在授权用途内，也就是只管资助活动（funded activities），考场意思：你拿这笔钱只能按项目目标花。
但政府不能借发钱之名，要求受补助者（funding recipients）放弃与项目无关的受保护言论（protected conduct），考场意思：钱只能管“这笔钱怎么用”，不能顺手管“你平时还能不能说话”。
本题的政治游说不属于修建、购置、维护演出设施这些被补助的用途，所以这条限制撞上第一修正案（First Amendment），并通过第十四修正案（Fourteenth Amendment）适用于各州。

核心判例： Agency for Int'l Dev. v. Alliance for Open Soc'y Int'l, Inc. — 政府不能把补助条件设成“你得先放弃与项目无关的受保护表达”。

思维导图

州政府给的补助条件，能不能直接卡住受款人的政治游说？
先看：这是不是只限制 funded activities？
能。政府可要求“这笔钱只能这么花”。
再看：还是在管 funding recipients 的其他受保护行为？
是。不能要求受款人放弃与项目无关的政治游说。
卡死点：游说不是这笔钱的使用方式，而是受款人的表达自由。
结论：第 1 和第 14 修正案攻击最强，选 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：政府既然在发补助，就可以顺便规定受款人别再做政治游说。
但考试真正问的是：这条条件是在管钱的用途，还是在管人的受保护表达。
司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干把补助和“不得从事政治游说”绑在一起，限制的是与设施资金无关的受保护表达，所以最强依据是第一和第十四修正案。

❌ 事实误判 | 市场参与偷换

✕ A: 把commerce clause拿来套发补助，方向就错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 联邦权利误认

✕ B: 这不是联邦对州的正当程序问题，Fifth Amendment本身不直打州法。

❌ 法律适用 | 合同条款误套

✕ D: 题干不是让州改已有合同，contracts clause对不上。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“管钱怎么花”还是“管你还能不能说”，再看受限行为是否超出项目范围。

考场速记

记忆口诀：政府能管资金用途（use of funds），不能逼受款人放弃与项目无关的第一修正案（First Amendment）表达。
遇到补助条件，先问“这是限定项目，还是限制人？”——如果是后者，优先想到 Agency for Int'l Dev. v. Alliance for Open Soc'y Int'l, Inc.。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
In one state, certain advanced diagnostic medical technologies were located only in hospitals, where they provided a major source of revenue. In many other states, such technologies were also available at "diagnostic centers" that were not affiliated with hospitals.
A group of physicians announced its plan to immediately open in the state a diagnostic center that would not be affiliated with a hospital. The state hospital association argued to the state legislature that only hospitals could reliably handle advanced diagnostic medical technologies. The legislature then enacted a law prohibiting the operation in the state of diagnostic centers that were not affiliated with hospitals.
The group of physicians filed suit challenging the constitutionality of the state law. What action should the court take?

choices.A: Dismiss the suit without reaching the merits, because the suit is not ripe.
choices.B: Invalidate the law, because it imposes an undue burden on access to medical services in the state.
choices.C: Uphold the law, because the legislature could rationally believe that diagnostic centers not affiliated with hospitals would be less reliable than hospitals.
choices.D: Uphold the law, because the provision of medical services is traditionally a matter of legitimate local concern that states have unreviewable authority to regulate.

questions.explanation:
Levels of scrutiny under equal protection clause
Severity of burden
Type of scrutiny

Rational basis

  • no rational relation to
  • legitimate state interest

Intermediate

  • substantial relation to
  • important state interest

Strict

  • necessary to achieve
  • compelling state interest
= challenger's burden = state's burden

The constitutionality of a discriminatory law can be challenged under the equal protection clause. Such challenges are generally reviewed under the rational basis test, which requires that the law be rationally related to any legitimate state interest. And since any reasonable, conceivable purpose that may have motivated the legislature to pass the law will satisfy this test, laws subject to the rational basis test are usually upheld.

Here, a state law discriminates against physicians who wish to operate an unaffiliated diagnostic center by requiring that diagnostic centers be affiliated with hospitals. Since the legislature could rationally believe that unaffiliated diagnostic centers would be less reliable than hospitals, the law is rationally related to a legitimate state interest—providing safe medical services. Therefore, the law satisfies the rational basis test and should be upheld.

(Choice A) A court will dismiss a suit without reaching the merits if it is not ripe—ie, if the plaintiff has yet to suffer actual harm or an imminent threat thereof. But since this law threatens the physicians' immediate plan to open a diagnostic center in the state, their suit is ripe for litigation.

(Choice B) Discriminatory laws that unduly burden a fundamental right are presumptively invalid and reviewed under strict scrutiny, which requires that the law be necessary to serve a compelling state interest. But access to medical services is not a fundamental right, so this law need only survive rational basis scrutiny.

(Choice D) State laws and regulations are always subject to constitutional limits, so the state does not have the unreviewable authority to regulate the provision of medical services—even if it is traditionally a matter of legitimate local concern.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the equal protection clause, discriminatory laws are generally reviewed under the rational basis test—ie, the law must be rationally related to any legitimate state interest. And any reasonable, conceivable purpose that may have motivated the legislature in passing the law will satisfy this test.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).
  • Heller v. Doe, 509 U.S. 312, 319–20 (1993) (explaining that any reasonable, conceivable legislative purpose will satisfy rational basis scrutiny).
  • Barsky v. Board of Regents, 347 U.S. 442, 449 (1954) (finding that a state has broad power to regulate the health profession).
questions.zh-question:
在某个州，某些先进的诊断医疗技术仅设于医院内，并成为医院的主要收入来源。在许多其他州，此类技术也可在不隶属于医院的“诊断中心”使用。

一群医生宣布了他们的计划，即刻在该州开设一家不隶属于医院的诊断中心。州医院协会向州立法机关主张，只有医院才能可靠地操作先进的诊断医疗技术。立法机关随后颁布了一项法律，禁止在该州经营不隶属于医院的诊断中心。

该群医生提起诉讼，挑战该州法律的合宪性。法院应采取何种行动？

zh-choices.A: 驳回诉讼，不对案情实质进行审理，因为该诉讼尚不成熟。
zh-choices.B: 宣布该法律无效，因为它对在该州获取医疗服务施加了不当负担。
zh-choices.C: 维持该法律，因为立法机关可以合理地认为，不隶属于医院的诊断中心比医院的可靠性更低。
zh-choices.D: 维持该法律，因为提供医疗服务传统上是地方正当关切的事项，各州对此拥有不可审查的监管权力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - State Taxation Of Commerce

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州法把非医院附属的诊所一刀切禁掉时，是否只要能过 平等保护（Equal Protection） 下的 理性基础审查（rational basis review） 就行。

三秒认题路径：

州限制开业 → 不是基本权利 → 看 rational basis → 合理目的即可 → 选 C

核心法律规则

如果州法不是碰到 基本权利（fundamental right），也不是对 可疑分类（suspect classification） 下手，MBE 默认先看 rational basis。考场意思：政府只要能拿出一个 合法州利益（legitimate state interest），而且法律和这个目的有 合理关联（rationally related），通常就能过。

这里州议会可以合理相信：不附属于医院的诊断中心可能没那么可靠，影响病人安全，所以禁令和“提供安全医疗服务”这个目的连得上。学生要抓住：这题不是问医院好不好，也不是问医疗服务重不重要，而是问州有没有一个说得通的理由。

核心判例： Heller v. Doe — 只要立法目的属于可想象的合理目的，rational basis 通常就会通过。

思维导图

州法禁“非医院附属诊所”
第1问：有没有碰到基本权利？
没有：开诊所不是基本权利 → 不上 strict scrutiny
第2问：有没有可疑分类？
没有：不是种族/国籍等分类 → 进入 rational basis
第3问：州能不能说出合理目的？
可以：安全医疗服务 + 觉得医院更可靠
卡死结论：
只要“说得通”就够 → 法律通常有效 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州把非医院诊所全禁了，看起来是在妨碍病人看病，应该很不公平。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是触发了更高审查，还是只要州能讲出一个合理的安全理由就够了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的禁令目标是医院附属，州只要合理担心独立诊所不够可靠，就满足 rational basis，所以应当维持。

❌ 概念混淆 | 期限起诉误判

✕ A: 把 ripeness 当主战场了，但题目已是现行禁令下的实体审查。

❌ 法律适用 | 严格审查套错

✕ B: 误以为医疗服务权受特别保护，但这里没有触发 strict scrutiny。

❌ 事实误判 | 绝对权力偷换

✕ D: 把州的监管权说成 unreviewable authority，这句话过头了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判审查等级，再看州有没有一个合理、可想象的安全目的。

考场速记

记忆口诀：rational basis 里，州只要能讲出“说得通”的合法目的，通常就过。

看到 平等保护（Equal Protection） 先问：是不是基本权利或可疑分类；不是的话，多半就是“合理关联 + 合法目的”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A public high school has had a very high rate of pregnancy among its students. In order to assist students who keep their babies to complete high school, the school has established an infant day-care center for children of its students, and also offers classes in child care. Because the child-care classes are always overcrowded, the school limits admission to those classes solely to students who are the mothers of babies in the infant day-care center.
A male student at the high school has legal custody of his infant son. The school provides care for his son in its infant day-care center, but will not allow the student to enroll in the child-care classes. He brings suit against the school challenging, on constitutional grounds, his exclusion from the child-care classes.
Which of the following best states the burden of persuasion in this case?

choices.A: The male student must demonstrate that the admission requirement is not as narrowly drawn as possible to achieve a substantial governmental interest.
choices.B: The male student must demonstrate that the admission requirement is not rationally related to a legitimate governmental interest.
choices.C: The school must demonstrate that the admission policy is substantially related to an important governmental interest.
choices.D: The school must demonstrate that the admission policy is the least restrictive means by which to achieve a compelling governmental interest.

questions.explanation:
Equal protection analysis
Was government action discriminatory?
(ie, treated similarly situated persons differently)
Yes
Default
↓
Rational basis test
Challenger must show
  • law is not rationally related to
  • legitimate state interest
Exception
↓
Government action substantially impacts:
Quasi-suspect class
  • Sex/gender*
  • Legitimacy
 
Suspect class
  • Ethnicity
  • Citizenship
  • Race
  • Nationality
 
Fundamental right
  • Voting
  • Interstate travel
  • Privacy
  • First Amendment right
Yes
↓
Intermediate scrutiny
State must show
  • law is substantially related to
  • important state interest
Strict scrutiny
State must show
  • law is necessary to achieve
  • compelling state interest
*State must also show an exceedingly persuasive justification.

A government action that treats similarly situated persons differently may be challenged under the equal protection clause. The action will only be deemed constitutional if there is adequate justification for the alleged discrimination. A law that discriminates based on gender or nonmarital birth (ie, quasi-suspect classes) is presumptively invalid unless it survives intermediate scrutiny—ie, the government demonstrates that the law is substantially related to an important government interest.

Here, a public high school offers child-care classes to students with children (government action). But enrollment is limited to female students with children in the school's infant day-care center (gender discrimination). And since the male student was excluded from these classes, the admission policy will only be found constitutional if the school meets its burden of persuasion under intermediate scrutiny.

(Choice A) The male student would have had the burden to prove that there was no adequate justification for the admission policy if rational basis review applied. And there is no burden of persuasion that requires proof that a government action be as narrowly drawn as possible to achieve a substantial government interest.

(Choice B) Generally, a challenger must prove that the government action does not rationally relate to a legitimate government interest (ie, rational basis review). But this burden of persuasion does not apply when the government action impacts a fundamental right, suspect class, or quasi-suspect class (as seen here).

(Choice D) The school would have had to demonstrate that the admission policy is the least restrictive means to achieve a compelling government interest (ie, strict scrutiny) had the policy impacted a fundamental right or suspect class. But here, the policy affected a quasi-suspect class (gender).

📌 Educational Objective

A government action challenged under the equal protection clause is subject to intermediate scrutiny if it discriminates against a quasi-suspect class (ie, sex/gender, nonmarital children). Intermediate scrutiny requires the government to prove that its action is substantially related to an important government interest.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (equal protection clause).
  • Craig v. Boren, 429 U.S. 190, 197 (1976) (holding that state discrimination based on sex/gender places the burden on the state to show that its action is substantially related to an important government interest).
questions.zh-question:
一所公立高中的学生怀孕率一直很高。为了帮助那些留下孩子并完成高中学业的学生，该学校为本校学生的孩子设立了一个婴儿日托中心，并提供育儿课程。由于育儿课程总是人满为患，学校将入学资格仅限于在学校婴儿日托中心有婴儿的母亲学生。

该高中的一名男学生拥有其幼子的合法监护权。学校在其婴儿日托中心为他的儿子提供照料，但不允许该男学生参加育儿课程。他以宪法为由对学校提起诉讼，质疑他被排除在育儿课程之外的决定。

以下哪项最能说明本案中的说服责任（burden of persuasion）？

zh-choices.A: 该男学生必须证明，该入学要求并非为实现某一重大的政府利益而尽可能地精准拟定。
zh-choices.B: 该男学生必须证明，该入学要求与合法的政府利益没有理性关联。
zh-choices.C: 学校必须证明，该招生政策与一项重要的政府利益有实质性关联。
zh-choices.D: 学校必须证明，该招生政策是为实现一项强制性的政府利益所采取的限制性最小的手段。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Equal protection

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：公立学校按性别（sex/gender）把学生挡在课程门外时，中度审查（intermediate scrutiny）下由谁承担证明责任。

三秒认题路径：

公校限制 → 按性别分 → 中度审查 → 学校举证 → 选 C

核心法律规则

平等保护（equal protection）先看政府是不是在对“相同处境的人”作差别待遇；如果是，再看用哪一档审查。

本题是性别（sex/gender）分类，考场意思：不是原告自己去证明学校没道理，而是政府要证明该政策与重要政府利益（important governmental interest）有实质关联（substantially related）。

所以这题的落点很窄：不是问学校政策“听起来合不合理”，而是问“burden of persuasion 谁来扛”。

核心判例： Craig v. Boren — 性别分类触发中度审查，政府要证明政策与重要政府利益之间有实质关联。

思维导图

公立学校按谁来限课？
先看：性别分类（sex discrimination），是 触发中度审查，不是理性基础审查
再问：谁来举证？
政府/学校 证明 政策与重要利益 实质关联
卡死点：原告不用证明“最不限制”或“完全不合理”；学校要扛中度审查的证明责任
结论：选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：学校是为了照顾带孩子的学生，听起来像“好政策”，所以应该让原告自己证明它不合理。

但考试真正问的是：一旦题干写出按性别限课，就别再用rational basis那套；要直接切到中度审查（intermediate scrutiny）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 只准“母亲”报名，是性别分类；中度审查下应由学校证明政策与重要政府利益有实质关联。

❌ 法律适用 | 最严标准误搬

✕ A: 把性别分类硬套成 narrowly drawn，这是一档错位。

❌ 概念混淆 | 理性审查反转

✕ B: 这是把性别歧视当成普通政策，让原告去扛 rationally related。

❌ 事实误判 | 以为是严格审查

✕ D: 题干只是性别分类，不是族裔或基本权利，别偷换成 compelling 标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认分类，再认审查等级，最后看谁承担证明责任。

考场速记

记住一句：性别分类（sex/gender）先想到中度审查（intermediate scrutiny），答案通常落在“政府证明实质关联”这一边。

口诀：sex = intermediate；看到“妈妈能报、爸爸不能报”，先问“谁来证明？”

question_analysis.skill_tested: Determining equal protection burden of persuasion

reason.en: Establishes the state action requirement necessary for an Equal Protection Clause challenge.

keywords.text: solely to students who are the mothers

reason.en: Identifies the core procedural question regarding who must prove the constitutionality and by what standard.

reason.en: Incorrectly shifts the burden of proof to the plaintiff challenger under intermediate scrutiny.
reason.zh: 在中级审查下错误地将证明责任转移给原告挑战者。

reason.en: Incorrectly applies the lowest tier of scrutiny, which is not applicable to gender discrimination.
reason.zh: 错误地适用了最低级别的审查标准，该标准不适用于性别歧视。

reason.en: Correctly places the burden of proof on the government (school) to justify gender classification.
reason.zh: 正确地将证明该性别分类合理性的证明责任置于政府（学校）一方。

reason.en: Applies the strict scrutiny requirement, which is only used for suspect classes or fundamental rights.
reason.zh: 适用了严格审查的要求，而严格审查仅用于可疑分类或基本权利。

reason.zh: 此限制基于性别进行歧视，从而适用中级审查。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Members of a religious group believe in Lucifer as their Supreme Being. The members of this group meet once a year on top of a mountain, located in a national park, to hold an overnight encampment and a midnight dance around a large campfire. They believe that this overnight encampment and ritual are required by Lucifer to be held on the top of that mountain. U.S. National Park Service rules that have been consistently enforced prohibit all overnight camping and all campfires on the mountain because of the very great dangers overnight camping and campfires would pose in that particular location. As a result, the park superintendent denied a request by the religious group for a permit to conduct these activities on top of the mountain. The park superintendent, who was known to be violently opposed to cults and other unconventional groups, had previously issued permits to conventional religious groups to conduct sunrise services in other areas of that national park.
The religious group brought suit in federal court against the U.S. National Park Service and the superintendent of the park to compel issuance of the requested permit.
As a matter of constitutional law, was the denial of the permit valid?

choices.A: No, because the free exercise clause of the First Amendment prohibits the Park Service from knowingly interfering with religious conduct.
choices.B: No, because these facts demonstrate that the action of the Park Service purposefully and invidiously discriminated against the religious group.
choices.C: Yes, because religiously motivated conduct may be subjected to nondiscriminatory time, place, and manner restrictions that advance important public interests.
choices.D: Yes, because the establishment clause of the First Amendment prohibits the holding of religious ceremonies on federal land.

questions.explanation:
Free speech analysis
Content-based restriction
(message, subject, or idea)
Strict scrutiny
(least restrictive means)
  • Necessary & narrowly tailored to compelling interest
Content-neutral restriction
(time, place, or manner)
Intermediate scrutiny
(no greater than necessary)
  • Narrowly tailored to substantial interest
  • Alternative avenues of communication
Exception
(nonpublic forum + viewpoint-neutral)
Rational basis
  • Reasonably related to legitimate interest

The permit denial restricts the religious group's right to free expression by preventing its religiously motivated conduct. However, the permit was denied because of a content-neutral (ie, nondiscriminatory) rule prohibiting all overnight camping and campfires on the mountain—not because of the content of the group's religious conduct. As a result, this time, place, or manner restriction is valid under intermediate scrutiny if it:

  • is narrowly tailored (ie, no greater than necessary) to serve a substantial or important government interest and
  • leaves open ample alternative channels of communication.

The park has an important interest in avoiding the "very great dangers" posed by overnight camping and campfires. And the park rule is narrowly tailored to that interest since (1) park safety would be compromised by allowing the prohibited activities and (2) there is no evidence that the group's conduct poses no such safety threat. The rule also provides alternative channels of communication since the group can conduct religious rituals at other times and places. Therefore, this speech restriction is valid.

The permit denial also interferes with the group's right to free exercise of religion, which largely prohibits intentional government interference with religion (Choice A). But an incidental interference is permissible if it is rationally related to a legitimate government interest. Here, the permit was denied under a generally applicable park rule (not the superintendent's beliefs), so the religious interference was incidental. And since the rule is rationally related to a legitimate interest in park safety, the permit denial complied with this right (Choice B).

(Choice D) The establishment clause prohibits the government from favoring a particular religion or religion generally. Therefore, religious ceremonies on federal land are permissible so long as the government remains neutral toward religion.

📌 Educational Objective

First Amendment free speech protections extend to religious conduct. But the government can impose content-neutral restrictions on such conduct so long as they (1) are narrowly tailored to serve an important government interest and (2) leave open ample alternative channels of communication.

📚 References
  • Clark v. Cmty. for Creative Non-Violence, 468 U.S. 288, 298–99 (1984) (holding that the denial of a camping permit for a demonstration is a constitutional time, place, and manner restriction on speech).
questions.zh-question:
一个宗教团体的成员信仰 Lucifer 为其至高无上的神。该团体的成员每年一次在一个国家公园内的山顶上聚会，举行通宵露营和围绕大篝火的午夜舞蹈。他们相信，Lucifer 要求他们在该山顶上举行这种通宵露营和仪式。U.S. National Park Service 的规定一贯禁止在该山上进行任何通宵露营和篝火，因为通宵露营和篝火在该特定地点会造成极大的危险。因此，公园负责人拒绝了该宗教团体在该山顶上进行这些活动的许可申请。该公园负责人以强烈反对邪教和其他非传统团体而闻名，此前曾向传统宗教团体颁发许可，允许其在该国家公园的其他区域举行日出仪式。

该宗教团体在联邦法院对 U.S. National Park Service 和该公园负责人提起诉讼，要求强制颁发所申请的许可。

从宪法角度看，拒绝颁发该许可的行为是否有效？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为第一修正案的自由行使条款禁止公园管理局故意干涉宗教行为。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为这些事实表明，公园管理局的行为是蓄意地、不公正地歧视该宗教团体。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为出于宗教动机的行为可能会受到非歧视性的时间、地点和方式限制，以促进重要的公共利益。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为第一修正案的政教分离条款禁止在联邦土地上举行宗教仪式。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation of speech

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：政府把宗教性活动当作 时间、地点、方式限制（time, place, or manner restriction） 来管时，能不能因为安全理由拒发许可。

三秒认题路径：

宗教活动 → 许可被拒 → 内容中立 → 中间审查 → 选 C

核心法律规则

这道题只看哪条规则

宗教性行为（religiously motivated conduct） 也可能受第一修正案保护，但政府若是按统一的安全规则来限制，就不是冲着观点去打压。内容中立限制（content-neutral restriction） 的考场意思：只要它是为了重要的政府利益、没有比必要更重，而且还留了别的表达路径，通常就能过。

这里真正问的不是“宗教能不能被管”，而是“这条登山过夜和生火禁令是不是对所有人都一样适用”。答案是：是，所以走 intermediate scrutiny，而不是 strict scrutiny。

核心判例： Clark v. Community for Creative Non-Violence — 许可拒绝基于普遍适用的露营禁令，属于合宪的 time, place, or manner 限制。

思维导图

先看：这条规则是在管“说什么”，还是只管“什么时候、哪里、怎么做”？
本题事实所有人都不能在山顶过夜、点营火；拒发许可是因为这条统一禁令，不是因为这群人的宗教内容。
第一关内容中立（content-neutral）
卡死点：不是针对“Lucifer”或宗教观点，而是针对山顶过夜和生火的危险。
第二关中间审查（intermediate scrutiny）
看三件事：重要政府利益、窄而必要、留有替代表达路径。
本题套用保护公园安全是重要利益；全面禁止高风险露营和营火是窄定向；宗教仪式还可在别处、别时举行。
结论许可拒绝有效，选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然这是宗教团体，政府一拒绝许可，好像就是在压制宗教。

但考试真正问的是：这条规则是不是对所有人都一样、是不是出于安全而不是针对宗教内容。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里最容易被带跑的是 自由行使条款（free exercise clause）。它不禁止所有间接影响宗教的中立规则；只要不是故意挑宗教下手，而且规则本身和合法利益有关，通常就能成立。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 统一禁止过夜和营火，说明这是对所有人都适用的内容中立规则；公园安全又是重要利益，所以可以作为合宪的时间、地点、方式限制。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“涉及宗教”直接等于“政府不能碰”，忽略了中立安全规则。

❌ 事实误判 | 故意歧视偷换

✕ B: 看到 superintendent 讨厌异端就认定是定向打压，题干真正决定结果的是统一禁令。

❌ 法律适用 | 建立条款误搬

✕ D: 把 establishment clause 误当成“联邦土地上不能做宗教活动”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓规则属性：内容中立还是内容针对；再看是否满足中间审查三要素。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先问是不是 内容中立（content-neutral），再看 中间审查（intermediate scrutiny）。如果是统一安全规则，通常就不是“宗教例外”，而是合法限制。

遇到许可、露营、营火、示威这类题，先想 time, place, or manner；能留替代路径、又服务重要利益，答案常常是“可以管”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A public university requires students to pay a student-activity fee that funds the activities of various student organizations. The university allocates these funds to student organizations without regard to their views.
A student organization received student-activity fee funds to hold a float parade. The organization rejected a student's float submission because the views espoused by the float were contrary to the organization's and parade's message. The student appealed the organization's decision to the university, but the university upheld the rejection of his submission.
The student has filed an action against the university, arguing that the university's decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the student's submission and the university's mandatory student-activity fee violate the First Amendment.
Are the university's actions constitutional?

choices.A: The decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the student's submission and the mandatory student-activity fee are constitutional.
choices.B: The decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the student's submission and the mandatory student-activity fee are unconstitutional.
choices.C: The decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the student's submission is constitutional but the mandatory student-activity fee is unconstitutional.
choices.D: The decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the student's submission is unconstitutional but the mandatory student-activity fee is constitutional.

questions.explanation:
First Amendment freedom not to speak
Type Examples
Impermissible
compulsion
  • Forcing students to salute flag or recite Pledge of Allegiance
  • Punishing motorists for covering state motto on license plates
  • Requiring private groups to include opposing viewpoints in their events
  • Requiring nonunion employees to pay public-sector union dues
Permissible
compulsion
  • Forcing public university students to pay activity fee if funds allocated in viewpoint-neutral manner
  • Requiring public shopping center to permit speech on property if speech not dictated by state & not identified with center's owner
  • Requiring lawyers to join bar association & pay dues to practice law

The First Amendment protects individuals' freedom to speak and their freedom not to speak. This means that the government and its subsidiaries (eg, public universities) cannot compel individuals to endorse or include viewpoints with which they disagree. Here, the student organization had the right to reject the student's float submission, and the university could not force the organization to accept that submission. Therefore, the university's decision to uphold the organization's rejection of the submission is constitutional (Choices B & D).

Additionally, the First Amendment generally prohibits the government and its subsidiaries from compelling individuals to financially support private speech with which they disagree.* However, there are limited exceptions to this rule, including that a public university can force its students to pay a student-activity fee if the funds are allocated in a viewpoint-neutral manner. Since the public university here allocates funds to student organizations without regard to their views, the mandatory student-activity fee is constitutional (Choices B & C).

*Individuals can be compelled to subsidize government speech through taxes because the First Amendment does not prohibit the government from using taxpayer funds to advocate for or defend its own policies or viewpoints.

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment protects the right to speak and not to speak. This means that the government cannot compel individuals to endorse, include, or financially support private speech with which they disagree. However, a public university can compel its students to pay an activity fee if the funds are allocated in a viewpoint-neutral manner.

📚 References
  • Hurley v. Irish-Am. Gay, Lesbian & Bisexual Grp. of Bos., 515 U.S. 557, 581 (1995) (holding that a state may not require private parade organizers to include messages they oppose in the parade).
  • Bd. of Regents of Univ. of Wisconsin Sys. v. Southworth, 529 U.S. 217, 234 (2000) (holding that a public university's mandatory student-activity fee is constitutional if the fee is allocated in a viewpoint-neutral manner).
  • 16A Am. Jur. 2d Constitutional Law §§ 471–73 (2020) (explaining when the First Amendment prohibits government-compelled speech).
questions.zh-question:
一所公立大学要求学生支付学生活动费，用于资助各类学生组织的活动。该大学在分配这些资金给学生组织时，不考虑其观点。

一个学生组织收到了学生活动费资金，用于举办花车游行。该组织拒绝了一名学生提交的花车方案，因为该花车所支持的观点与该组织及游行所要传达的信息相悖。该学生就该组织的决定向大学提出上诉，但大学维持了拒绝其方案的决定。

该学生对大学提起诉讼，主张大学维持该组织拒绝其方案的决定以及大学强制征收学生活动费的行为违反了 First Amendment（第一修正案）。

该大学的行为是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 维持该组织拒绝学生方案的决定以及强制征收学生活动费的行为均合宪。
zh-choices.B: 维持该组织拒绝学生方案的决定以及强制征收学生活动费的行为均违宪。
zh-choices.C: 维持该组织拒绝学生方案的决定合宪，但强制征收学生活动费的行为违宪。
zh-choices.D: 维持该组织拒绝学生方案的决定违宪，但强制征收学生活动费的行为合宪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation of speech

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：公立大学的学生活动费（student-activity fee）能否按观点中立（viewpoint-neutral）方式资助社团，以及学校是否能替社团强迫其接受相反观点。

三秒认题路径：

公立大学 → 活动费 → 观点中立 → 不强迫表态 → 选 A

核心法律规则

第一修正案（First Amendment）保护“能说”也保护“不被迫说（freedom not to speak）”，所以政府和其下属机构不能逼私人团体替自己塞进相反观点；但公立大学（public university）把学生活动费按观点中立（viewpoint-neutral）分配时，通常是合宪的。

考试上你要抓的是：这里不是问社团有没有理由拒收投稿，而是问大学有没有权把这件事改成“必须收”。答案是否定的，因为学校不能替社团强迫其表达。

核心判例： Hurley v. Irish-Am. Gay, Lesbian & Bisexual Grp. of Bos. 和 Bd. of Regents of Univ. of Wisconsin Sys. v. Southworth — 前者说不能强迫私人游行组织接纳相反信息，后者说活动费只要按观点中立分配就可以。

思维导图

先看大学做了什么：是“强迫表达”，还是“中立资助”？
第1关：学校是否逼私人团体接纳相反观点？
否。Hurley：私人组织有权拒绝与自己信息冲突的内容。
所以“维持组织拒稿”这一点是合宪。
第2关：学生活动费是否按观点中立分配？
是。公立大学只要不按立场挑人，就可以收这笔费。
这里卡死的是“观点不满 ≠ 违宪”。Southworth 允许中立资助。
结论：两个动作都过关，答案是 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然学生的浮板被拒了，感觉就是“被压制言论”，大学还帮忙维持，应该违宪。

但考试真正问的是：大学有没有把私人的编辑权（editorial control）抢过来强迫它收稿；这里没有，因为社团自己有权拒绝相反观点。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干写明活动费按viewpoint-neutral 分配，且学校不能强迫社团接受相反信息，所以两项都合宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ B: 把“社团可拒稿”当成“大学也违法”，是把两层主体混在一起。

❌ 法律适用 | 中立标准误读

✕ C: 误以为viewpoint-neutral 只要有资助就违宪，其实中立分配正是合宪条件。

❌ 事实误判 | 强迫对象偷换

✕ D: 看到“拒绝投稿”就想成学校在逼学生发言，实际上被逼的是社团吗？不是。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是谁在被迫表达，再看活动费是否按观点中立分配，最后直接锁定结论。

考场速记

记住一句：私人组织的编辑权不能被政府夺走；但公立大学活动费只要按观点中立分配，通常就能过关。

碰到这类题，先问“谁被迫说话”，再问“钱是不是中立发”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
On the basis of scientific studies showing a causal relationship between the consumption of "red meat" (principally beef) and certain forms of cancer, a federal statute prohibits all commercial advertising of red-meat products. The statute does not, however, restrict the sale of red-meat products. Producers of red meat have challenged the statute as a violation of their free speech rights protected by the First Amendment.
Is the court likely to find the statute constitutional?

choices.A: No, because it does not serve a substantial government interest.
choices.B: No, because it is more extensive than necessary to serve the government interest in preventing certain cancers.
choices.C: Yes, because it does not affect speech protected by the First Amendment.
choices.D: Yes, because it serves a legitimate government interest in protecting public health.

questions.explanation:
Regulation of commercial speech
Does speech concern false/misleading
information or unlawful activity?
No
↓
Does regulation directly advance
substantial government interest?
No
→
Invalid
regulation
Yes
↓
Is regulation more extensive than
necessary to serve interest?
Yes

Invalid
regulation
No

regulation

The government can ban commercial speech that (1) is false or misleading or (2) concerns unlawful activity. But all other commercial speech is protected by the First Amendment, albeit to a lesser extent than other forms of expression (eg, political speech). This means that the government can only regulate protected commercial speech if the government proves that its regulation directly advances a substantial government interest and is not more extensive than necessary to serve that interest.

Here, the red-meat advertisements are protected commercial speech since there is no evidence that they are false or misleading and red meat is a lawful product (Choice C). And the statute prohibiting these advertisements likely advances the government's substantial interest in protecting the public from certain cancers (Choice A). But the statute is more extensive than necessary to achieve that interest since a cancer warning in those advertisements (instead of a total ban) would suffice. Therefore, the statute will likely be found unconstitutional.

(Choice D) A legitimate government interest is never sufficient to justify the regulation of protected speech.

📌 Educational Objective

The government can only regulate protected commercial speech if the regulation (1) directly advances a substantial government interest and (2) is not more extensive than necessary to serve that interest.

📚 References
  • Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n, 447 U.S. 557, 564 (1980) (providing the test for determining whether the government's regulation of protected commercial speech is constitutional).
questions.zh-question:
根据显示食用“红肉”（主要是牛肉）与某些形式的癌症之间存在因果关系的科学研究，一项联邦法规禁止所有红肉产品的商业广告。然而，该法规并不限制红肉产品的销售。红肉生产商已对该法规提出质疑，认为其侵犯了受第一修正案保护的言论自由权。

法院是否可能裁定该法规合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为它不符合重大的政府利益。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为其范围超出了为实现预防某些癌症的政府利益所必需的程度。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为它不影响受第一修正案保护的言论。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为它服务于保护公共健康的合法政府利益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation Of Content

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：受保护的商业言论（commercial speech）能不能被政府一刀切禁掉；答案看 Central Hudson test，重点卡在“是不是比必要范围更大”。

三秒认题路径：

商业广告 → 受保护言论 → 直接促进利益 → 是否过宽 → 不能

核心法律规则

商业言论（commercial speech）如果不是虚假/误导，也不涉及违法活动，就受第一修正案保护，只是保护力度比政治言论低。政府要限制这种受保护商业言论，必须证明两步：一是限制 directly advances 重大政府利益，二是不能比实现该利益所必需的范围更大。这里政府保护公众免受某些癌症风险，利益本身够重；但“全面禁止红肉广告”比“加警示语”更狠，所以卡在第二步。

核心判例： Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp. v. Public Service Commission — 这题就是用它的商业言论四步框架，最后死在“不得过度限制”这一步。

思维导图

先看这是不是受保护的商业言论？
否 若属虚假、误导或违法交易，可直接限制
是
政府限制能否过关？
1 是否 directly advances 重大政府利益？本题里“防癌”大概率能过。
2 是否 more extensive than necessary？全面禁广告太狠，警示语就够了。
结论 第二步没过 → 法规无效 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然政府有科学研究证明红肉和癌症有关，那它当然能直接禁广告。

但考试真正问的是：它有没有用 commercial speech 的标准把手伸太长了，不是它有没有一个听起来正当的公共健康理由。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 all commercial advertising 属于过宽限制；政府就算要防癌，也不能把整类受保护商业言论一刀切封死。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“政府利益”误当成不够重，其实这里更像substantial interest已经成立了。

❌ 法律适用 | 受保护范围误判

✕ C: 看到是广告就说不受保护，漏了商业广告本来就可能受第一修正案保护。

❌ 事实误判 | 利益层级偷换

✕ D: 把 legitimate government interest 当成够用，但受保护商业言论要的是更高门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判定是不是受保护商业言论，再按 Central Hudson 依次查“利益够不够重”和“限制有没有过宽”。

考场速记

记住一句：商业言论不是“能管就随便管”，而是要过 Central Hudson 的双关卡；一旦发现“全面禁掉”比“警示语”更狠，通常就是过宽。

口诀：先看是不是受保护商业言论，再看是否直接促进重大利益，最后问有没有比必要范围更大。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state adopted a rule denying admission to its bar to anyone who was currently or had previously been a member of a subversive group. The state's bar-application form was then modified to ask applicants whether they were or had previously been members of any subversive organization. An applicant refused to answer the question and was denied bar admission on that basis. The applicant challenged the decision, arguing that the question infringed upon his freedom of association.
Is the applicant likely to prevail?

choices.A: No, because membership in a subversive group constitutes endorsement of the group's illegal activities.
choices.B: No, because the Constitution does not apply to the bar.
choices.C: Yes, because a broad inquiry into an applicant's association with a subversive organization as a possible basis to deny bar admission violates the First Amendment unless it is necessary to protect a legitimate state interest.
choices.D: Yes, because denying bar admission based on any association with a subversive organization violates the First Amendment.

questions.explanation:
Freedom of association
(inquiry & punishment)
Inquiry about a person’s
associations
  • inquiry is necessary to further
  • legitimate state interest
No→Unconstitutional
Yes
Punishment for association with
subversive organization
  • active member
  • knows of illegal objectives
  • specifically intends to further objectives
No→Unconstitutional
Yes
Constitutional

The First Amendment protects the right to freely associate with any group or organization—including subversive organizations. As such, the government cannot inquire about a person's associations for the sole purpose of withholding a right or benefit because of that person's beliefs. Instead, the government must show that the inquiry is necessary (i.e., the least restrictive means) to protect a legitimate state interest. As a result, a state may deny bar membership to a candidate who refuses to answer questions about her knowing membership in a subversive group only if that refusal obstructs the investigation of the candidate's qualifications.

Here, an applicant was denied bar admission for refusing to answer whether he was or had been a member of any subversive organization. This question—like the associated rule—relates to the state's legitimate interest in ensuring that applicants have the requisite character and professional competence to practice law. But that interest can be protected through less restrictive means—e.g., requiring a list of references and other professional information. Additionally, the broad inquiry is not limited to the applicant's knowing membership in a subversive group. As a result, he is likely to prevail.

(Choice A) Membership in a subversive group does not necessarily constitute endorsement of the group's illegal activities since the individual may have joined for other, nonsubversive reasons. The individual also may have tentatively agreed with the group's goals when he became a member but then rejected their activities.

(Choice B) The Constitution (excluding the Thirteenth Amendment) applies only to government action. The rule at issue here constitutes government action since it was adopted by the state. Therefore, the Constitution applies.

(Choice D) The government may punish individuals (e.g., by denying bar admission) who are active members of subversive organizations and have the specific intent to further the organizations' illegal activities.

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment prohibits the government from inquiring into a person's associations unless that inquiry is necessary to protect a legitimate state interest.

📚 References
  • Baird v. State Bar of Ariz., 401 U.S. 1, 6–7 (1971) (holding that a state can only inquire about a person's associations if it is necessary to serve a legitimate state interest).
questions.zh-question:
某个州通过了一项规则，拒绝授予律师资格给任何当前或曾经是颠覆性组织成员的人。该州的律师资格申请表也相应修改，询问申请人当前或曾经是否是任何颠覆性组织的成员。一名申请人拒绝回答该问题，并因此被拒绝授予律师资格。该申请人对该决定提出质疑，主张该问题侵犯了他的结社自由。

该申请人是否可能胜诉？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为成为颠覆性组织的成员即构成对该组织非法活动的认可。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为宪法不适用于律师协会。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为基于与颠覆性组织的任何关联而拒绝授予律师资格违反了第一修正案。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为为拒绝授予律师资格而调查申请人与颠覆性组织的关联，这违反了第一修正案。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation of association

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府能不能用“协会背景询问（inquiry into associations）”去筛掉报考律师的人；答案是，除非这项询问对保护合法州利益（legitimate state interest）必不可少，否则不行。

三秒认题路径：

州问社团 → 拒答被拒 → 第一修正案 → 需正当目的 → 选 C

核心法律规则

第一修正案保护结社自由（freedom of association），所以政府不能只是因为“我想知道你跟谁来往”就广泛盘问。

只有当这种询问对查明资格、维护合法州利益（legitimate state interest）是必要的，而且没有更温和的方法时，州才可以问。

这里的考场意思很直接：州不是不能审查律师资格，但它不能把“你以前是不是成员”当成一把过宽的筛子，尤其当还有参考人、职业经历等更窄的方式可用时。

核心判例： Baird v. State Bar of Arizona — 州只有在询问确实必要时，才可以追问申请人的社团关联。

思维导图

先看州的动作：这是在问“你有没有加入过某个组织”吗？
是 这是协会询问（inquiry into associations），先问：它是不是为了查资格真的必要？
否 直接卡死：不能只为剥夺利益而广泛盘问
结论：此类过宽询问通常违宪
是 再看内容：它是否只聚焦于知情成员（knowing membership）和资格审查？
否 本题失败点：问题太宽，不限于必要范围
答案走向：选 C，不选 D
是 这才可能合宪；但本题题干没有做到这一步。
补一刀 “问得越宽” ≠ “审查越正当”

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是“subversive organization”，那政府当然可以直接拒绝，毕竟加入这种团体看起来像是在支持非法活动。

但考试真正问的是：州能不能先问、问多宽、有没有更窄的方式；不是在问这个人“道德上坏不坏”。

这题看的是「法律上是否必要」，不是「你直觉上觉得可疑不可疑」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 bar-application form 要求广泛回答是否曾属任何组织，但州利益可用更窄手段保护，所以这种询问过宽，通常违反第一修正案。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把membership直接当成支持非法活动，偷换了“加入”与“认同”的区别。

❌ 事实误判 | 政府行为忽略

✕ B: 这不是私人规则，题干明确是州改表格问话，government action 早就成立。

❌ 法律适用 | 处罚范围扩大

✕ D: 它把“任何关联”都说成可罚，但本题是过宽询问，不是已经证明其有特定违法意图。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓政府是否在“问关联”，再看这问题是不是必要且够窄；只要过宽，就先怀疑违宪。

考场速记

记住一句：结社题先看“问得是否必要”，不是先看组织名头吓不吓人。

口诀可记为：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是上诉例外常用口令；但本题更关键的是“必要才可问”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city ordinance requires every taxicab operator in the city to have a license and permits revocation of that license only for "good cause." The ordinance conditions the issuance of such a license on an agreement that the licensee "not display in or on his or her vehicle any bumper sticker or other placard or sign favoring a particular candidate for any elected municipal office." The ordinance imposes this condition to prevent the possible imputation of the views of taxicab licensees onto the city council, and it states that any licensee who violates this condition shall have his or her license revoked.
A driver who holds a taxicab operator's license decorates his cab with bumper stickers and other signs favoring specified candidates in a forthcoming election for municipal offices. A proceeding is initiated against him to revoke his taxicab operator's license on the sole basis of that admitted conduct.
In this proceeding, does the driver have a meritorious constitutional defense?

choices.A: No, because a taxicab operator's license is a privilege and not a right and, therefore, is not protected by the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.B: No, because he accepted the license with knowledge of the condition and, therefore, has no standing to contest it.
choices.C: Yes, because such a proceeding threatens the driver with a taking of property, his license, without just compensation.
choices.D: Yes, because the condition imposed on taxicab operators' licenses restricts political speech based wholly on its content, without any adequate governmental justification.

questions.explanation:

The city ordinance infringes upon the First Amendment right to free expression by conditioning the issuance of a license on the driver's promise not to display signage favoring political candidates. The ordinance regulates speech based on its content (ie, message, subject, or ideas), so it is presumptively invalid and only enforceable if it survives strict scrutiny. This requires the government to prove that the ordinance is necessary and narrowly tailored (ie, the least restrictive means) to achieve a compelling government interest.

Here, the city may have a compelling interest in avoiding the imputation of drivers' views onto the city council. But since that interest can be achieved through less restrictive means—eg, by requiring drivers to display a disclaimer—the ordinance cannot survive strict scrutiny. As a result, the driver has a meritorious constitutional defense against his license being revoked based solely on his violation of this invalid ordinance.

(Choice A) The Supreme Court no longer distinguishes between a privilege and a right when considering challenges under the Fourteenth Amendment due process clause.

(Choice B) The driver did not waive his constitutional right to engage in political speech by accepting the license with knowledge of the signage condition. Therefore, the driver does have standing to contest the revocation of his license.

(Choice C) The Fifth Amendment takings clause only requires the payment of just compensation when the government takes private property for public use, so it does not apply here.

📌 Educational Objective

Content-based speech regulations must pass strict judicial scrutiny. This requires proof that the regulation is necessary and narrowly tailored to achieve a compelling government interest.
questions.zh-question:
一项城市条例要求该市的每位出租车运营者都必须持有执照，并规定只有在有“正当理由”的情况下才能撤销该执照。该条例规定，签发此类执照的条件是，持照人同意“不在其车辆内或车辆上展示任何支持特定民选市政公职候选人的保险杠贴纸或其他标语牌或标志”。该条例施加此条件，是为了防止出租车持照人的观点可能被归咎于市议会，并规定任何违反此条件的持照人，其执照将被撤销。

一名持有出租车运营执照的司机，用支持即将举行的市政公职选举中特定候选人的保险杠贴纸和其他标志来装饰其出租车。一项程序已对他启动，旨在仅基于他所承认的这一行为而撤销其出租车运营执照。

在此程序中，该司机是否有理据的宪法抗辩？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为出租车运营执照是一种特权而非权利，因此不受《Fourteenth Amendment》正当程序条款的保护。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为他在知晓该条件的情况下接受了执照，因此没有诉讼资格对其提出异议。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为此等程序对司机构成了对其财产（即其执照）的征收威胁，而没有给予公正的补偿。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为对出租车运营执照施加的条件完全基于其内容来限制政治言论，而没有任何充分的政府理由。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation Of Content

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：政府能不能用牌照条件，直接禁止政治表态这种内容型限制（content-based restriction）。

三秒认题路径：

政治标语 → 内容限制 → 严格审查 → 不能最少限制 → 选 D

核心法律规则

政治言论属于受保护言论（protected speech），考场意思：政府一旦按“说了什么内容”来管，就先站在劣势。

内容型限制（content-based restriction），考场意思：只要规则盯着信息主题或观点下手，就要过严格审查（strict scrutiny）。

严格审查要求政府证明：它有重大利益（compelling interest），而且是最少限制手段（least restrictive means）。这题里，即使城市担心“观点被误认为是市议会的”，也可以用免责声明，没必要直接禁政治贴纸。

核心判例： 这题的逻辑就是严格审查那一套：内容型政治言论限制，除非真的是最少限制手段，否则保不住。

思维导图

先看：这是按内容管言论吗？
YES禁止“支持某候选人”的标语，直接盯住政治观点。
规则政治言论 + 内容限制 → 严格审查（strict scrutiny）。
政府要同时证明：重大利益（compelling interest） + 最少限制手段（least restrictive means）。
卡死点：这里不是“有没有理由”，而是“能不能不用这么狠的禁令”。
可用免责声明就能降低误认风险，所以直接禁贴纸太重。
结论先例外没过，撤销牌照条款站不住。
答案：D
如果是内容中立的时间、地点、方式限制，才可能走较轻审查。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：司机是拿执照做事，政府就能附条件管他。

但考试真正问的是：它是不是在用执照条件，直接打掉政治内容本身。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这里别被“牌照”“城市管理”带偏，真正要看的还是内容型言论审查能不能过严格审查。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 禁止支持候选人的标语 是按内容管政治言论，必须过严格审查；这里有更温和的免责声明手段，所以不能通过。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把执照当成免责盾牌，忽略了言论自由照样受审查。

❌ 法律适用 | 放弃权利误判

✕ B: 看到 accepted the license 就说放弃宪法权利，太跳步。

❌ 事实误判 | 赔偿对象偷换

✕ C: 把言论限制硬扯成征收财产，题干根本不是政府拿走财产。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认定是否内容型限制，再直接套严格审查，看政府有没有更温和的替代手段。

考场速记

记住：政治言论一旦被内容型限制，先问strict scrutiny，再问政府有没有更轻的办法；有更轻办法，通常就输。

这一题的口令就是：内容型限制（content-based restriction） → 严格审查（strict scrutiny） → 看最少限制手段（least restrictive means）。

D.text: restricts political speech based wholly on its content

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state in which several popular ski resorts are located has enacted a law requiring state certification of ski instructors. Under the law, applicants for certification must attend a monthlong course, pass a test, and pay a fee of $1,000. The stated purpose of the law is to "promote uniformity in the methods of ski instruction at the state's ski areas."
Shortly before the law's enactment, when the state did not require certification of ski instructors, a woman moved to the state intending to find employment as a ski instructor. The woman had been a ski instructor in another state for many years. But since her move, even though ski resorts in the state have found her to be highly qualified, no resort will offer her a contract for employment as a ski instructor because she has not received the required state certification.
As applied to the woman, does the state certification requirement constitute a violation of the contracts clause?

choices.A: No, because her ability to contract for employment with the state is not being impaired.
choices.B: No, because she has no existing contract that is being impaired.
choices.C: Yes, because as applied to an otherwise qualified ski instructor, the requirement is not rationally related to a legitimate government interest.
choices.D: Yes, because the requirement substantially impairs her ability to contract for employment in the absence of an important government objective.

questions.explanation:
Contracts clause analysis
Does plaintiff have existing contract?
No
Constitutional
Does new state law substantially
impair contract?
No
Constitutional
Yes
Private contract
(more deference to state)
Public contract
(less deference to state)
Is impairment reasonable & narrowly tailored
to important & legitimate public interest?
Yes
Constitutional
Unconstitutional
The contracts clause restricts state laws—not court decisions or federal legislation—that substantially impair existing contracts. Therefore, this clause does not apply to future contracts.

Here, the state law interferes with the woman's ability to obtain an employment contract as a ski instructor. But since she has not been hired by a ski resort, the law does not impair any existing contract. Therefore, the state certification requirement does not violate the contracts clause as applied to the woman.

(Choice A) The contracts clause applies to private contracts (ie, agreements with non-government parties) and public contracts (ie, agreements with government entities). But the woman's ability to contract for employment with the state is irrelevant since this clause only protects existing contracts.

(Choices C & D) The contracts clause would only apply if the woman—qualified or not—had an existing contract. And had one existed, a substantial impairment of that contract would only be upheld if it was reasonable and narrowly tailored (not just rationally related) to an important and legitimate government interest (here, promoting uniformity in ski-instruction methods in the state).

📌 Educational Objective

The contracts clause restricts state laws that substantially impair existing (not future) contracts.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. art. I, § 10 (contracts clause).
  • Gen. Motors Corp. v. Romein, 503 U.S. 181, 186 (1992) (explaining that the contracts clause only applies when a state law substantially impairs an existing contractual relationship).
questions.zh-question:
一个拥有数个热门滑雪胜地的州颁布了一项法律，要求滑雪教练必须获得州级认证。根据该法律，申请认证者必须参加为期一个月的课程、通过一项考试并支付1000美元的费用。该法律宣称的目的是“促进本州滑雪区滑雪教学方法的一致性”。

在该法律颁布前不久，当该州还不要求滑雪教练认证时，一名女子搬到该州，打算找一份滑雪教练的工作。这名女子在另一个州当了很多年的滑雪教练。但自从她搬来后，尽管该州的滑雪胜地认为她非常合格，却没有一家滑雪胜地愿意向她提供滑雪教练的雇佣合同，因为她没有获得所要求的州级认证。

就适用于这名女子的情况而言，该州的认证要求是否构成了对合同条款的违反？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为她与州政府签订雇佣合同的能力并未受到损害。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为她没有现存的合同受到损害。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为就适用于一名在其他方面合格的滑雪教练而言，该要求与合法的政府利益之间没有合理的关联。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为在没有重要的政府目标的情况下，该要求严重损害了她签订雇佣合同的能力。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Obligation of contracts

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：契约条款（Contracts Clause）只管州法是否削弱已有合同，不管你只是以后想签合同却还没签成。

三秒认题路径：

州法来了 → 先看有无旧合同 → 没有旧合同 → 直接不违宪 → 选 No

核心法律规则

契约条款（Contracts Clause）只限制州法对既有合同的重大干预，考场意思：先问“有没有已经存在的合同关系”，没有就不用继续做后面的平衡。

如果只是未来想签 employment contract（雇佣合同），但现在还没有雇主和你达成合同，州法就只是影响你将来能不能签，不是直接破坏现成合同。

只有先有合同，再看州法是否 substantially impair（实质性削弱）；到了那一步，才会继续问州法是否有重要且正当的公共目的，以及手段是否合理且狭窄。

核心判例： General Motors Corp. v. Romein —— 契约条款只在州法实质性削弱既有合同关系时才启动。

思维导图

先问：题干有没有既有合同？
NO直接结束：契约条款不启动，答案走 No。
题干只说她想找 ski instructor（滑雪教练） 工作，但还没有被任何度假村雇用，所以没有现成合同可被州法“削弱”。
YES 才继续看：州法是否 substantially impair（实质性削弱）？
再看：有没有重要且正当的公共目的？
最后才看：手段是否合理、是否狭窄。
本题卡死点：没有既有合同，所以不进入后面的重要目的测试。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州法让她现在不能当滑雪教练，看来合同自由被限制了。

但考试真正问的是：有没有一份已经存在、正在被州法削弱的合同；这题里她只是想未来签约，还没有现成合同。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是她还没和任何度假村形成现有雇佣合同，所以州法没有在削弱一份既有合同，契约条款不成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 合同对象错位

✕ A: 只盯着她能否和州雇主签约，混淆了“想缔约”与“已有合同受损”。

❌ 法律适用 | 理由门槛错套

✕ C: 把“理性相关”搬来这里，但契约条款先卡的是有没有既有合同。

❌ 事实误判 | 现有合同漏读

✕ D: 把“她找不到工作”偷换成“合同已被削弱”，题干根本没这一步。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序姿态：有没有既有合同；没有就立刻停，不必进入后面的公共目的分析。

考场速记

记住一句：契约条款（Contracts Clause）只管“已有合同被州法削弱”，不管“未来能不能签上合同”。

本题口诀：先找旧合同，再谈实质削弱；没旧合同，直接选 No。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
Several sites on a mountain within federal public lands are regarded as sacred to a group of people that has gathered there for years to perform religious ceremonies. The United States Forest Service recently issued a permit to a private developer to construct a ski facility in an area that includes the sites that are sacred to the group.
The group has filed suit in federal district court against the Forest Service to force cancellation of the permit, claiming solely that the permit violates its First Amendment right to the free exercise of religion. The Forest Service has conceded that the group's religious beliefs are sincere and that construction of the ski facility will adversely affect the group's religious practices.
What must the group show to prevail on its First Amendment claim?

choices.A: Construction of the ski facility will have a discriminatory impact on the group's religious practices in relation to the practices of other religious groups.
choices.B: The burden on the group's religious practices that will be imposed by construction of the ski facility outweighs the government's interest in allowing the facility.
choices.C: The government can serve its legitimate interest in allowing the ski facility by issuing a permit that is less burdensome on the group's religious practices.
choices.D: The permit issued by the government is aimed at suppressing the religious practices of the group.

questions.explanation:
Explanation
First Amendment free exercise of religion
Burden Applicability Level of scrutiny
Incidental Generally applicable to all persons Rational basis scrutiny:
  • burden rationally related to
  • legitimate government interest
Direct Intentionally targets religious belief/practice Strict scrutiny:
  • burden necessary to achieve
  • compelling government interest

The United States Forest Service issued a permit for the construction of a ski facility on land sacred to a religious group. As a result, the group filed suit to cancel the permit since the construction would adversely affect its First Amendment right to perform religious ceremonies. The group's likelihood of success depends on whether that burden is either:

• incidental – triggering rational basis scrutiny, where the challenger will fail unless the challenger shows that the burden has no rational relation to any legitimate government interest or

• direct – triggering strict scrutiny, where the challenger will prevail unless the government meets the nearly impossible task of showing that the burden is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest.

Therefore, to have the greatest chance of prevailing on its First Amendment claim, the group must show that the government-issued permit is aimed at suppressing (ie, directly burdens) the group's religious practices.

(Choice A) The ski facility's discriminatory impact on the group's religious practices allows the group to bring a free exercise claim. But that claim will likely fail unless the group can show that the discriminatory impact was intentional, which would create a presumption of invalidity that would be difficult for the government to rebut.

(Choice B) A free exercise challenge will be analyzed under rational basis or strict scrutiny, neither of which weighs the burden on religion against the government's interest.

(Choice C) To prevail, the group must show that the permit directly burdens its religious practices. Once it does so, the burden shifts to the government to show that its compelling (not merely legitimate) interest in the ski facility cannot be achieved by less burdensome means.

📌 Educational Objective

Incidental burdens on the free exercise of religion are typically upheld under rational basis review. But direct burdens are almost always invalidated under strict scrutiny.

📚 References
  • Emp't Div. v. Smith, 494 U.S. 872, 878–79 (1990) (establishing the direct/incidental burden test).
  • Church of Lukumi Babalu Aye v. City of Hialeah, 508 U.S. 520, 546 (1993) (applying strict scrutiny to a city ordinance that intentionally targeted a religious practice).
