一项联邦刑事法律规定，对于知悉或有理由知悉通讯内容系被非法录制，而故意公布该通讯内容的个人，将处以刑罚。

一个教师工会和一个学校董事会正在就一份集体谈判协议进行充满争议的谈判。该教师工会的一名成员在学校董事会主席的电话上非法安装了窃听器。该教师工会成员匿名将主席几次关于谈判的电话交谈录音寄给了一位当地电台脱口秀主持人。该脱口秀主持人在一个没有任何回邮地址、发件人信息或标签的盒子里收到了这些录音。在听完录音后，该脱口秀主持人在她的节目中播放了这些录音。在交谈中，主席发表了一些贬损性和令人尴尬的言论。

一名检察官随后对该电台脱口秀主持人提起指控，因其在节目中播放录音违反了该联邦法律。该电台脱口秀主持人声称该联邦法律违宪。

根据该联邦法律对该电台脱口秀主持人的起诉是否可能合宪？

zh-choices.A: 不合宪，因为该联邦法律是一种事先限制。
zh-choices.B: 不合宪，因为该主持人并非非法获取录音，也不知道是谁获取的。
zh-choices.C: 合宪，因为私人电话交谈不属于公众关注的事务。
zh-choices.D: 合宪，因为该主持人知悉该录音系非法获取。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation Of The Media

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：媒体发布 第三方非法录得但公众关注的信息 时，第一修正案能不能挡住联邦刑责。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否公开传播 → 再看是否公共关注 → 再看发布者是否合法取得 → 结论：通常可免责

核心法律规则

第一修正案（First Amendment）一般保护媒体发布 真实信息（truthful information），只要内容涉及 公共关注事项（matter of public concern）。如果信息是第三人非法录得的，媒体仍可能受保护，但前提是媒体自己是 合法取得（lawfully obtained） 这些材料的人。换句话说，考场上不是问“信息有没有被偷录”，而是问“这家媒体自己拿到它时，站不站得住”。

核心判例： Bartnicki v. Vopper — 第三方非法取得、但媒体合法取得且内容属公共关注的信息，通常不能仅因播放而处罚媒体。

思维导图

先问：这题是不是“发布真实信息后的事后处罚”
是终局前禁令？不是。这里是事后刑罚，不是先禁止发表。
信息来源第三人非法录得，但媒体不是偷录的人。
内容属性和集体谈判有关，属于 公共关注事项（matter of public concern）。
关键卡口媒体是否自己 合法取得（lawfully obtained）？是
结论若媒体合法接收并播放，Bartnicki 逻辑下通常不能处罚。
答案走向：B 选项抓住“host did not unlawfully obtain”这一步

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然录音是偷偷来的，播出去的人也该一起罚。

但考试真正问的是：媒体自己有没有非法获取；这里她只是收到匿名包裹后播放，不能把“知道来路可疑”直接等同于“自己非法取得”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 匿名送达 且主持人并未亲自窃录，媒体是合法取得后播放；内容又涉及集体谈判这一公共关注事项，所以不能仅因播出而定罪。

❌ 法律适用 | 先后关系误判

✕ A: 把事后处罚硬说成 prior restraint，方向错了。

❌ 概念混淆 | 公共关注误判

✕ C: 以为私人电话就一定没公共性，漏掉了劳资谈判本身是新闻议题。

❌ 事实误判 | 知情偷换

✕ D: 题干最多说她可能知道来路可疑，不等于她自己 unlawfully obtained。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“谁非法取得”与“谁只是合法接收后发布”，再看内容是否属于公共关注。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Bartnicki 先看“公共关注 + 合法取得”；别人偷来的，不一定能罚媒体，关键看媒体自己是不是偷来的那一个。

遇到媒体发布、隐私录音、公共议题这类题，先别被“恶心感”带跑，直接问：who obtained it unlawfully?

reason.zh: 表明该法律是在发布后施加处罚，而非事先限制。

reason.en: The prosecution punishes completed publication and does not prevent speech before publication.
reason.zh: 该起诉处罚已经完成的发布，并未在发布前阻止言论。

B.text: did not unlawfully obtain the recordings

reason.en: States the critical condition for First Amendment protection when a third party made the illegal interception.
reason.zh: 指出第三方非法截获时适用第一修正案保护的关键条件。

C.text: not a matter of public concern

reason.en: The collective-bargaining negotiations are newsworthy and therefore concern the public.
reason.zh: 集体谈判具有新闻价值，因而属于公共关注事项。

D.text: knew that the recordings were unlawfully obtained

reason.en: Knowledge of third-party illegality does not establish that the host herself obtained the recordings unlawfully.
reason.zh: 知道第三方行为违法，并不表明主持人本人非法取得录音。

highlights.text: contentious negotiations over a collective-bargaining agreement

reason.en: The newsworthy subject of the conversations satisfies the public-concern requirement.
reason.zh: 谈话涉及具有新闻价值的主题，满足公共关注事项要件。

reason.en: Identifies someone other than the publisher as the party responsible for the unlawful acquisition.
reason.zh: 表明非法取得信息者并非发布者本人。

highlights.text: played them on her show

reason.en: Triggers First Amendment analysis of liability for publishing truthful information.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city's personnel handbook contains all of that city's personnel policies. One section of the handbook states that "where feasible and practicable supervisors are encouraged to follow the procedures specified in this handbook before discharging a city employee." Those specified procedures include a communication to the employee of the reasons for the contemplated discharge and an opportunity for a pre-termination trial-type hearing at which the employee may challenge those reasons.
After a year of service, the secretary to the city council was discharged without having received any communication of reasons for her contemplated discharge and without having received an opportunity for a pre-termination trial-type hearing.
The former secretary files suit in federal district court to challenge her discharge solely on constitutional grounds.
Which of the following best describes the initial burden of persuasion in that suit?

choices.A: The city council must demonstrate that its personnel handbook created no constitutionally protected interest in city employment or in the procedures by which such employment is terminated.
choices.B: The city council must demonstrate that the former secretary's termination was for good cause.
choices.C: The former secretary must demonstrate that she reasonably believed that she could work for the city for as long as she wished.
choices.D: The former secretary must demonstrate that state law creates a constitutionally protected interest in her employment or in the procedures by which her employment is terminated.

questions.explanation:
The former secretary's claim raises the Fourteenth Amendment right to procedural due process, which requires states and municipalities to follow certain procedures when they intentionally deprive a person of life, liberty, or property. These procedures include giving persons:

  • notice of the charges, proceedings, or other actions against them and
  • a meaningful opportunity to be heard by a neutral decision-maker.

In a due process claim, the challenging party has the initial burden of showing that he/she has a protected life, liberty, or property interest at stake. Therefore, the former secretary must demonstrate that state law created a constitutionally protected interest in her employment or the procedures by which she was terminated (Choice A).

(Choice B) The city council would only need to demonstrate that the former secretary's termination was for good cause if she first demonstrates that she has a constitutionally protected interest in her employment.

(Choice C) Public employees have a property interest in their jobs if they (1) have an ongoing employment contract, (2) can only be fired for cause, or (3) receive assurances of continued employment. But the former secretary's reasonable belief that she could work for the city as long as she wished would not create this interest.

📌 Educational Objective

Procedural due process requires the government to follow certain procedures when it intentionally deprives a person of life, liberty, or property. And in a due process claim, the challenger has the initial burden of showing that he/she has a protected interest at stake.

📚 References
  • Cleveland Bd. of Educ. v. Loudermill, 470 U.S. 532, 538 (1985) (holding that a state cannot terminate an employee without due process when the employee has a property right in his/her employment).
questions.zh-question:
某市的员工手册包含了该市所有的人事政策。手册中有一节规定，「在可行和切实的情况下，鼓励主管在解雇市政雇员之前，遵循本手册中规定的程序。」这些规定的程序包括：向雇员告知计划解雇的理由，并提供一次解雇前审讯式听证会的机会，雇员可以在听证会上对这些理由提出质疑。

在服务一年后，市议会的秘书被解雇，但她并未收到任何关于计划解雇理由的通知，也未获得解雇前审讯式听证会的机会。

该前任秘书在联邦地区法院提起诉讼，完全基于宪法理由对其解雇提出质疑。

以下哪项最能描述该诉讼中的初步说服责任？

zh-choices.A: 市议会必须证明，其员工手册并未在市政雇佣关系中或在终止此类雇佣关系的程序中，创设任何受宪法保护的利益。
zh-choices.B: 市议会必须证明，解雇前任秘书是基于正当理由的。
zh-choices.C: 前任秘书必须证明，她有合理理由相信，只要她愿意，就可以一直为该市工作。
zh-choices.D: 前任秘书必须证明，州法律在其雇佣关系中或在终止其雇佣关系的程序中，创设了一项受宪法保护的利益。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Procedural Due Process Applied

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：程序性正当程序（procedural due process）里，原告先要证明自己有受保护的财产权或自由权，负举证责任不在政府。

三秒认题路径：

先看有权利 → 再看州法 → 先由原告举证 → 再谈程序缺失 → 选 D

核心法律规则

程序性正当程序（procedural due process）考的是：政府要剥夺一个人的life, liberty, or property，先要给notice和opportunity to be heard。但考试第一步不是先骂政府没给程序，而是先问原告有没有被州法（state law）保护的利益。

所以这题里，前秘书要先证明州法让她对这份工作，或对解雇程序，本身有了受保护的财产利益。没有这个门槛，就谈不上政府必须给她预先告知和听证。

核心判例： Cleveland Bd. of Educ. v. Loudermill —— 只有先有受保护的就业财产利益，政府解雇前才必须给程序。

思维导图

先问：原告有没有受保护的 property interest？
有 州法、合同、for-cause 约束、持续就业保证，才进入正当程序审查。
没有 直接卡死：政府不给预先程序，也不构成这题里的宪法违法。
本题谁先举证？
原告先证 先证明州法创造了受保护利益，再讨论是否缺少 notice 和 hearing。
政府后答 不是政府先证明“有原因”或“程序够不够”。
考试结论
答案 选 D：先由前秘书证明州法创设了受保护的就业利益。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然手册写了预先通知和听证，市政府就该先证明自己有理由解雇。

但考试真正问的是：前秘书有没有先跨过“受保护利益”这道门槛；没跨过去，政府根本不需要先自证。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键是先证明州法创造受保护利益；前秘书必须先有财产性就业利益，才轮到讨论预先告知和听证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 举证顺序错位

✕ A: 把举证责任倒给政府，混淆了先证明权利再谈程序。

❌ 法律适用 | 原因审查误判

✕ B: good cause 不是第一步，先有受保护利益才谈解雇理由。

❌ 事实误判 | 主观期待偷换

✕ C: 只凭“我以为能一直干下去”不够，主观期待不能自己造出财产权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓程序姿态：原告是否先证明受保护利益，再看政府有没有给 notice 和 hearing。

考场速记

记住一句：先权利，后程序；先利益，后告知。 本题就是先问州法有没有给你可被宪法保护的工作利益。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state enacted a statute providing for the closure of the official state records of arrest and prosecution of all persons acquitted of a crime by a court or against whom criminal charges were filed and subsequently dropped or dismissed. The purpose of this statute is to protect these persons from further publicity or embarrassment relating to those state proceedings. However, this statute does not prohibit the publication of such information that is in the possession of private persons.
A prominent businessman in the state was arrested and charged with rape. Prior to trial, the prosecutor announced that new information indicated that the charges should be dropped. He then dropped the charges without further explanation, and the records relating thereto were closed to the public pursuant to the state statute. A newspaper in the state conducted an investigation to determine why the businessman was not prosecuted but was refused access to the closed official state records.
In an effort to determine whether the law enforcement agencies involved were properly doing their duty, the newspaper filed suit against appropriate state officials to force opening of the records and to invalidate the statute on constitutional grounds.
Which of the following would be most helpful to the state in defending the constitutionality of this statute?

choices.A: The argument that the rights of the press are no greater than those of citizens generally.
choices.B: The argument that the state may seal official records owned by the state on any basis its legislature chooses.
choices.C: The fact that the statute only prohibits public access to these official state records and does not prohibit the publication of information they contain that is in the possession of private persons.
choices.D: The fact that the statute treats in an identical manner the arrest and prosecution records of all persons who have been acquitted of a crime by a court or against whom criminal charges were filed and subsequently dropped or dismissed.

questions.explanation:
There is no constitutional right to access government information. Therefore, the government can deny the public (and media) access to official state records. But since there is a First Amendment right to publish truthful information, any government restriction on this right is unconstitutional unless it survives strict scrutiny—ie, the government proves that the restriction is necessary to achieve a compelling government interest. Therefore, the fact that the statute only prohibits public access to state records and does not prohibit the publication of information they contain would help the state defend the statute's constitutionality.

(Choice A) The argument that the press has no greater rights than citizens generally, while true, merely shows that the same standard applies to claims by the press and ordinary citizens. But it does not explain why the newspaper's claim will fail.

(Choice B) A state may seal its official records on any legal or constitutional basis—not any basis that its legislature chooses.

(Choice D) The fact that the statute treats the records of all persons charged with, but not convicted of, a crime identically shows that the statute complies with the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. But this fact will not help the state because it does not address the First Amendment issue—accessing and publishing those records.

📌 Educational Objective

Although there is no right to access government information, there is a First Amendment right to publish truthful information. As a result, any government restriction on this right is unconstitutional unless it survives strict scrutiny.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. I (free press).
  • Houchins v. KQED, Inc., 438 U.S. 1, 14–15 (1978) (holding that there is no constitutional right to access government information).
questions.zh-question:
某一州颁布了一项法规，规定封存所有被法院宣告无罪，或被提起刑事指控但随后被撤销或驳回的人的官方逮捕和起诉记录。该法规的目的是保护这些人免受与这些州级诉讼程序相关的进一步宣传或尴尬。然而，该法规并不禁止公布私人持有的此类信息。

该州一位知名商人因强奸罪被逮捕和起诉。在审判前，检察官宣布新信息表明应撤销指控。随后，他在没有进一步解释的情况下撤销了指控，相关记录根据州法规对公众关闭。该州一家报纸进行了一项调查，以确定该商人为何未被起诉，但其查阅已封存的官方州记录的请求被拒绝。

为了确定相关执法机构是否正当履行其职责，该报纸对相应的州政府官员提起诉讼，要求强制公开记录，并以违宪为由宣告该法规无效。

以下哪一项最有助于州政府为该法规的合宪性进行辩护？

zh-choices.A: 主张新闻界的权利不大于普通公民的权利。
zh-choices.B: 主张州政府可以根据其立法机构选择的任何基础，封存其拥有的官方记录。
zh-choices.C: 该法规仅禁止公众查阅这些官方州记录，但并不禁止公布私人持有的、这些记录中所包含的信息这一事实。
zh-choices.D: 该法规以相同方式对待所有被法院宣告无罪，或被提起刑事指控但随后被撤销或驳回的人的逮捕和起诉记录这一事实。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation Of The Media

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府能不能封存官方记录，同时又不禁止私人持有者继续发表真实信息；考场上关键是区分“能不能拿到政府档案”和“能不能发表内容”。

三秒认题路径：

封存公文 → 媒体求取 → 先看访问权 → 再看发表权 → 选 C

核心法律规则

只需抓住这一条

访问政府信息（access to government information）没有独立的宪法权利；所以州政府可以拒绝公众和媒体查阅官方记录，Houchins v. KQED就是这个意思。

但发表真实信息（publish truthful information）受第一修正案保护；如果政府要限制发表，就得过严格审查（strict scrutiny）。所以本题里，最帮州政府的点不是“不给看”，而是“只是封官方档案，并没有禁止私人手里的信息被发表”。

核心判例： Houchins v. KQED, Inc. - 说明公众没有要求进入或查阅政府记录的宪法权利，所以州可以关档案室，但不能顺手把发表真实信息的问题说成访问权问题。

思维导图

先问：新闻媒体要的是“看政府记录”，还是“发真实信息”？
第一关：有没有访问政府信息（access to government information）的宪法权利？
没有。州可拒绝公开官方记录，终点不是立刻违宪。
第二关：州法有没有直接禁掉发表真实信息（publish truthful information）？
如果只是封官方档案，但没禁私人持有的内容继续发表，攻击点就弱很多。
第三关：本题州法的关键保护点是什么？
只限制公众查阅官方记录，不限制私人信息的发表。
所以最有帮助的是 C。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然记者为了查清真相，州就应该开放记录，所以只要说“媒体有更强的知情权”就能赢。

但考试真正问的是：州有没有把发表真实信息（publish truthful information）也一起禁掉。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题的陷阱是把“拿不到政府文件”误当成“不能发表信息”。前者州通常能做，后者才真正碰到第一修正案。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的statute only prohibits public access只是在封官方记录，没有禁止私人已知内容的发表；这正好避开了第一修正案对真实信息发表的直接打击。

❌ 概念混淆 | 访问权误认

✕ A: 只说媒体和普通人一样，没有抓到“访问权本来就不存在”。

❌ 法律适用 | 任意封存误判

✕ B: 看到 any basis 就乱放权，但州封档案也得过宪法审查。

❌ 事实误判 | 平等对待偷换

✕ D: 只是在讲一视同仁，没回应媒体能不能看、能不能发。

这题建议用什么方法？

先拆成“能不能访问政府记录”和“能不能发表真实信息”两步，再看州法到底禁了哪一步。

考场速记

记住一句：没有访问政府信息的宪法权利，但有发表真实信息的第一修正案保护。所以本题先找“州只是封档案，还是连发表也禁了”。

口诀：“能不让你看，不等于能不让你发。”

question_analysis.skill_tested: Distinguish access rights from publication rights

keywords.text: closure of the official state records

label.en: denial of access to government records

reason.en: Triggers the rule that the Constitution generally provides no right to access government information.
reason.zh: 触发宪法通常不保障查阅政府信息权利的规则。

reason.en: Shows that the statute regulates access rather than the First Amendment right to publish truthful information.
reason.zh: 表明该法限制的是查阅，而非第一修正案保护的真实信息发布权。

reason.en: Places the businessman's records within the category sealed by the statute.
reason.zh: 使该商人的档案属于法律规定的封存范围。

reason.en: Identifies the precise governmental action challenged by the newspaper.
reason.zh: 明确报社所挑战的具体政府行为。

reason.en: Confirms that the newspaper was denied access, not restrained from publishing information already obtained.
reason.zh: 确认报社被拒绝的是查阅，而非发布已取得的信息。

keywords.text: to force opening of the records

reason.en: Shows that the requested relief concerns access to government information.
reason.zh: 表明所请求的救济涉及查阅政府信息。

A.text: rights of the press are no greater than those of citizens generally

label.en: equal press and public access rights

reason.en: This true principle does not establish why the access restriction itself is constitutional.
reason.zh: 该原则虽正确，却不能说明查阅限制本身为何合宪。

B.text: on any basis its legislature chooses

reason.en: Overstates state authority because sealing decisions must still comply with constitutional requirements.
reason.zh: 夸大州的权力，因为封存决定仍须符合宪法要求。

reason.en: Directly invokes the distinction between unprotected access and protected publication.
reason.zh: 直接体现不受保障的查阅与受保障的发布之间的区别。

reason.en: Preserves the First Amendment right to publish truthful information already possessed.
reason.zh: 保留发布已掌握真实信息的第一修正案权利。

C.text: in the possession of private persons

reason.en: Clarifies that information obtained independently may still be published.
reason.zh: 说明通过独立途径取得的信息仍可发布。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.topic: Power To Enforce The Thirteenth, Fourteenth, And Fifteenth Amendments (Civil War Amendments)
questions.question:
The constitution of State X authorizes a five-member state reapportionment board to redraw state legislative districts every ten years. In the last state legislative reapportionment, the board, by a unanimous vote, divided a greater metropolitan area composed of a city and several contiguous townships into three equally populated state legislative districts. As a result of that districting, 40% of the area's total black population resided in one of those districts, 45% of the area's total black population resided in the second of those districts, and 15% resided in the third district.
A black resident of the greater metropolitan area is a registered voter. He filed suit in the appropriate court against the members of the state reapportionment board, seeking declaratory and injunctive relief that would require the boundary lines of the state legislative districts in the greater metropolitan area to be redrawn. His only claim is that the current apportionment violates the Fifteenth Amendment and the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment because it improperly dilutes the voting power of black residents in that area.
If no federal statute is applicable, which of the following facts, if proven, would most strongly support the validity of the action of the state reapportionment board?

choices.A: Although the rate of voter registration among black residents is below that of voter registration among white residents in the greater metropolitan area, two minority-preferred legislators were elected from that area during the last 15 years.
choices.B: In drawing the current district lines, the reapportionment board precisely complied with state constitutional requirements that state legislative districts be compact and follow political subdivision boundaries to the maximum extent feasible.
choices.C: The reapportionment board was composed of three white members and two black members, and the black board members were satisfied that the plan did not improperly dilute the voting power of black residents residing in that area.
choices.D: The total black population of the greater metropolitan area amounts to only 15% of the population that is required to comprise a single legislative district.

questions.explanation:
The Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause ensures that each citizen is given equal voting power (i.e., one person, one vote) by requiring state legislative districts to have largely equal populations. And the Fifteenth Amendment ensures that the right to vote is not abridged on account of race. Therefore, race cannot be the predominant factor used to draw boundary lines for state legislative districts. If it is, the boundary lines will be strictly scrutinized and likely deemed unconstitutional.

Here, the state reapportionment board created three equally populated state legislative districts. These districts have varying black populations and may improperly dilute the voting power of black residents in those areas. But race would not be the predominant factor behind redistricting if the board drew these boundaries to comply with state constitutional requirements that districts be compact and follow political subdivision boundaries. In that case, the board's action would be valid.

(Choice A) The Voting Rights Act (not the Constitution) requires that jurisdictions maintain a minority's ability to elect preferred candidates. But the question stipulates that this federal statute does not apply. And even if it did, the prior election of minority-preferred legislators could invalidate the board's action if the redistricting impaired black voters' ability to continue electing these candidates. But the rate of voter registration is irrelevant.

(Choice C) Had the board been predominantly motivated by the improper dilution of minority voting power (i.e., race), neither its composition nor its black members' satisfaction with the plan could validate the redistricting. But an argument that the board was motivated by other, non-racial factors would support its redistricting action.

(Choice D) Although the metropolitan area's black population is only 15% of the population required for a legislative district, the validity of a redistricting plan is not impacted by how the area's minority population compares to the population required for a district. Therefore, this fact has no bearing on the validity of the board's action.

📌 Educational Objective

Race cannot be the predominant factor used to draw boundary lines for state legislative districts. And if it is, those boundary lines will be subject to strict scrutiny and likely invalidated on equal protection grounds.

📚 References
  • Miller v. Johnson, 515 U.S. 900, 916 (1995) (explaining that the use of race as a predominant factor in drawing state legislative districts should be strictly scrutinized).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Power To Enforce The Thirteenth, Fourteenth, And Fifteenth Amendments (Civil War Amendments)

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州立法选区重划时，种族（race）能不能成为主导因素；如果是，通常会触发严格审查并很危险。

三秒认题路径：

重划选区 → 看主因 → 若是种族 → 严格审查 → 选 B

核心法律规则

第十四修正案平等保护（equal protection clause）要求州立法选区大体等人数，不能把种族（race）当成划线的主导因素；第十五修正案（Fifteenth Amendment）禁止因种族而剥夺投票权。

所以，考场上你要先问：这套边界是不是主要为了照顾种族？如果不是，而是为了州宪法要求（state constitutional requirements），例如紧凑和尽量沿政治分区划分，方案更容易站得住。

这题只要证明“不是种族主导”，就能帮州方守住行动；不需要把黑人选民比例、历史背景或政治情绪讲成主轴。

核心判例： Miller v. Johnson - 说明在州立法选区重划中，若种族是主导因素，就会被严格审查。

思维导图

州立法选区划线时，真正主导的是谁？
先看：是不是为了种族（race）去画线？
如果是主导因素 → 严格审查 → 很危险。
再看：有没有非种族理由支撑？
如果是为了紧凑（compact）和政治分区边界（political subdivision boundaries） → 说明种族不是主因。
落点：题干给出三个人口均等选区，关键不是“有没有黑人分散”，而是“划线理由是什么”。
结论：能证明按州宪法标准划线 → 选区行动有效 → 选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：黑人选民被分散了，voting power 好像被稀释了，所以一定违宪。

但考试真正问的是：州划线时有没有把种族当成主导因素，而不是结果看起来对谁不利。

这题里，VRA（Voting Rights Act）并没有适用；别把“少数群体能否持续选出偏好候选人”的问题，偷换成宪法本身自动禁止的结论。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是按州宪法要求保持紧凑并尽量沿政治分区划线，这给出的是非种族理由，所以更能支持该重划方案有效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 Voting Rights Act 的思路硬搬进来。

❌ 法律适用 | 族裔同意误判

✕ C: 委员里有黑人、黑人委员也满意，不代表划线理由就合格。

❌ 事实误判 | 人口比例偷换

✕ D: 把黑人总人口只占一个选区的人口门槛，误当成合法性标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓重划目的，再看有没有种族主导；只要有非种族划线理由，就优先保住州方。

考场速记

记住一句：选区重划看主因，不看表面结果。种族如果只是附带效果，通常没那么容易倒；如果是主导因素，就要警惕严格审查。

这题顺手记住 Miller v. Johnson：race as predominant factor 是红旗。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city zoning ordinance requires that anyone who proposes to operate a group home obtain a special-use permit from the city zoning board. The zoning ordinance defines a group home as a residence in which four or more unrelated adults reside.
An individual applied for a special-use permit to operate a group home for convicted felons during their transition from serving prison sentences to their release on parole. Although the proposed group home met all of the requirements for the special-use permit, the zoning board denied the individual's application because of the nature of the proposed use.
The individual sued the zoning board seeking declaratory and injunctive relief on constitutional grounds.
Which of the following best states the appropriate burden of persuasion in this action?

choices.A: Because housing is a fundamental right, the zoning board must demonstrate that denial of the permit is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.
choices.B: Because the zoning board's action has the effect of discriminating against a quasi-suspect class in regard to a basic subsistence right, the zoning board must demonstrate that the denial of the permit is substantially related to an important government interest.
choices.C: Because the zoning board's action invidiously discriminates against a suspect class, the zoning board must demonstrate that denial of the permit is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.
choices.D: Because the zoning board's action is in the nature of an economic or social welfare regulation, the individual seeking the permit must demonstrate that the denial of the permit is not rationally related to a legitimate government interest.

questions.explanation:
State and municipal (eg, city) government actions that treat similarly situated persons differently (ie, discriminate) can be challenged under the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. To comply with this clause, the challenged action must satisfy the appropriate level of scrutiny:

  • rational basis scrutiny (default test) – the challenger has the burden to prove that the government action is not rationally related to a legitimate government interest
  • intermediate scrutiny (quasi-suspect class) – the government has the burden to prove that its action is substantially related to an important government interest or
  • strict scrutiny (fundamental right or suspect class) – the government has the burden to prove that its action is necessary to serve a compelling government interest.

Here, the zoning board denied the individual's application for a permit to operate a group home for convicted felons—even though the proposal met all the permit requirements. The denial was discriminatory because it was based solely on the nature of the individual's proposed use. But housing is not a fundamental right (Choice A), and convicted felons are not a quasi-suspect or suspect class (Choices B & C). As a result, the individual must show that this economic or social welfare regulation does not satisfy rational basis scrutiny.

📌 Educational Objective

Equal protection challenges that do not involve a fundamental right, quasi-suspect class, or suspect class are reviewed under rational basis scrutiny. This level of scrutiny requires the challenger to show that the government action is not rationally related to a legitimate government interest.

📚 References
  • City of Cleburne v. Cleburne Living Ctr., Inc., 473 U.S. 432, 439–41 (1985) (explaining that discriminatory economic and social regulations are analyzed under rational basis scrutiny).
questions.zh-question:
一个城市区划条例要求，任何提议经营集体之家的人都必须从城市区划委员会获得特殊用途许可。该区划条例将集体之家定义为四个或四个以上无亲属关系的成年人居住的住所。

一个人申请了特殊用途许可，以经营一个为服刑人员在服刑期满过渡到假释期间所设立的集体之家。尽管拟议的集体之家满足了特殊用途许可的所有要求，但区划委员会因其拟议用途的性质而拒绝了个人的申请。

该个人以宪法为由起诉了区划委员会，寻求宣告性救济和禁令性救济。

在此诉讼中，以下哪项最能说明适当的说服责任？

zh-choices.A: 因为住房是一项基本权利，区划委员会必须证明，拒绝许可是为实现一项紧迫的政府利益所必需的。
zh-choices.B: 因为区划委员会的行为在基本生计权方面具有歧视准可疑分类的效果，区划委员会必须证明，拒绝许可是与一项重要的政府利益有实质性关联的。
zh-choices.C: 因为区划委员会的行为对一个可疑分类构成了恶意歧视，区划委员会必须证明，拒绝许可是为实现一项紧迫的政府利益所必需的。
zh-choices.D: 因为区划委员会的行为本质上属于经济或社会福利法规，申请许可的个人必须证明，拒绝许可与一项合法的政府利益没有理性关联。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Nonsuspect classifications

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：平等保护（Equal Protection）下，普通市政分区/许可规则遇到既非基本权利（fundamental right）也非可疑/准可疑分类（suspect/quasi-suspect class）时，要走最低审查（rational basis review），而且举证通常压在挑战者身上。

三秒认题路径：

分区许可 → 非基本权利 → 非可疑分类 → 最低审查 → 挑战者举证

核心法律规则

州和市政府对同类人作不同处理时，会先看用哪一档审查。最低审查（rational basis review）的考场意思：政府只要有一个正当政府利益（legitimate government interest）的理性连接，通常就能过关；要打掉它，必须证明这条规定连这个门槛都没到。

如果碰到基本权利（fundamental right）或可疑分类（suspect class），才会上到严格审查（strict scrutiny）；如果是准可疑分类（quasi-suspect class），才会走中间审查（intermediate scrutiny）。这题里，住房（housing）不是基本权利，已定罪重罪犯（convicted felons）也不是可疑或准可疑分类，所以还是回到最低审查。

核心判例： City of Cleburne v. Cleburne Living Center, Inc. — 说明对群体之家/分区限制这类经济与社会福利规制，若不碰基本权利或可疑分类，默认用最低审查。

思维导图

题干事实
群体之家拿到了所有形式要件，却被按“用途性质”拒绝。
先问分类
不是基本权利，也不是可疑/准可疑分类。
审查档位
普通经济或社会福利规制 → 最低审查（rational basis）。
卡死结论
挑战者必须证明“not rationally related”，所以选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是住房、又带有排斥性，就该直接上严格审查（strict scrutiny）。

但考试真正问的是：这条规则有没有碰到基本权利（fundamental right）或可疑分类（suspect class）；没有的话，还是先回到普通的经济/社会规制框架。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「政策看起来多不公平」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干是市政分区下的群体之家许可争议，convicted felons 既不是可疑分类，housing 也不是基本权利，所以由挑战者证明没有理性关系。

❌ 概念混淆 | 基本权利误判

✕ A: 把住房硬说成fundamental right，想直接拉到严格审查。

❌ 法律适用 | 准可疑类误套

✕ B: 先认定成quasi-suspect class，但重罪犯不在这一档。

❌ 事实误判 | 可疑分类偷换

✕ C: 把定罪身份偷换成suspect class，题干根本没给这种地位。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是否触发基本权利或可疑分类，再决定是不是把举证压回挑战者。

考场速记

记住这句：没有基本权利、没有可疑分类，就先想 rational basis；政府赢面大，通常是挑战者去证明“这规定连理性关系都没有”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state legislature received complaints from traffic accident victims who, in the days immediately following their accidents, had received unwelcome and occasionally misleading telephone calls on behalf of medical care providers. The callers warned of the risks of not obtaining prompt medical evaluations to detect injuries resulting from accidents and offered free examinations to determine whether the victims had suffered any compensable injuries.
In response to these complaints, the legislature enacted a law prohibiting medical care providers from soliciting any accident victim by telephone within 30 days of his or her accident.
Which of the following arguments would be most helpful to the state in defending the constitutionality of the law?

choices.A: Because the commercial speech that is the subject of the law includes some speech that is misleading, the First Amendment does not limit the state's power to regulate that speech.
choices.B: Because the law regulates only commercial speech, the state need only demonstrate that the restriction is rationally related to achieving the state's legitimate interests in protecting the privacy of accident victims and in regulating the medical profession.
choices.C: The law is a reasonable time, place, and manner regulation.
choices.D: The state has substantial interests in protecting the privacy of accident victims and in regulating the practice of medical care providers, and the law is narrowly tailored to achieve the state's objectives.

questions.explanation:
First Amendment speech protections

Commercial speech that (1) is false or misleading or (2) concerns unlawful activity does not fall under First Amendment protection and can be freely regulated by the government. But all other commercial speech is entitled to an intermediate level of First Amendment protection. This means that the government can only regulate protected commercial speech if the government proves that its regulation directly advances a substantial government interest and the regulation is narrowly tailored to achieve that interest.

Here, the state law prohibits medical care providers from soliciting accident victims by telephone within 30 days of the accident. The phone calls are protected commercial speech since they are only occasionally misleading (ie, most are truthful) and do not concern unlawful activity (Choice A). As a result, the state's best argument is that it has substantial interests in protecting the privacy of accident victims and in regulating the practice of medical care providers, and the law is narrowly tailored to achieve those objectives (Choice B).

(Choice C) The law is not a time, place, and manner regulation (ie, content-neutral restriction) since it prohibits phone calls based on what is being said (ie, content-based restriction).

📌 Educational Objective

Commercial speech that is not false or misleading and does not concern unlawful activity receives First Amendment protection. And any government regulation of that speech must (1) directly advance a substantial government interest and (2) be narrowly tailored to achieve that interest.

📚 References
  • Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n, 447 U.S. 557, 564 (1980) (providing the test for determining whether the government's regulation of protected commercial speech is constitutional).
questions.zh-question:
某州立法机构收到了交通事故受害者的投诉，这些受害者在事故发生后的几天内，接到了代表医疗服务提供者的不受欢迎且偶尔带有误导性的电话。致电者警告说，不及时进行医疗评估以检测事故造成的伤害存在风险，并提供免费检查以确定受害者是否遭受了任何可获赔偿的伤害。

为回应这些投诉，该立法机构颁布了一项法律，禁止医疗服务提供者在事故发生后30天内通过电话招揽任何事故受害者。

以下哪项论点最有助于州政府为该法律的合宪性进行辩护？

zh-choices.A: 由于该法律所规制的商业言论包含一些误导性言论，因此First Amendment并不限制州政府规制该言论的权力。
zh-choices.B: 由于该法律仅规制商业言论，州政府只需证明该限制与实现其保护事故受害者隐私和监管医疗行业的合法利益有合理关联。
zh-choices.C: 该法律是一项合理的时间、地点和方式的规制。
zh-choices.D: 州政府在保护事故受害者的隐私和监管医疗服务提供者的执业行为方面拥有重大利益，并且该法律是为实现州政府目标而狭义定制的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Regulation Of Content

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府能不能管住商业言论（commercial speech），以及它要过中度审查（intermediate scrutiny）这道门。

三秒认题路径：

商业电话 → 非违法 → 非虚假 → 受保护 → 中度审查

核心法律规则

这题只要抓住这条线

商业言论（commercial speech）如果不是虚假或误导（false or misleading），也不涉及违法活动（unlawful activity），就受第一修正案保护，不能被州政府随便一句“我想管”直接压下去。

这类言论适用中度审查（intermediate scrutiny），考场意思：州政府必须证明它的限制directly advances一个重大政府利益（substantial government interest），而且手段要narrowly tailored。

本题里的电话推销只是“有时让人不放心”，但并没有被题干说成整体都在骗人，也没有涉及违法活动，所以不能按“无保护言论”处理。

核心判例： Cent. Hudson Gas & Elec. Corp. v. Pub. Serv. Comm'n —— 它把受保护商业言论的审查标准钉死为“重大利益 + 直接推进 + 窄限手段”。

思维导图

先看这是不是 商业言论（commercial speech）？
是，而且题干说的是 “劝你去做医疗检查”的电话推销。
再看它是不是虚假/误导或涉及违法活动？
不是整体都落空： 题干只说“偶尔误导”，主线仍是受保护商业言论。
所以能不能直接禁？
不能只靠情绪： 先过中度审查（intermediate scrutiny）。
卡死点：州必须同时证明substantial interest + narrowly tailored
本题州方最强论点
保护隐私 + 监管医疗职业， 且 30 天禁拨是围着目标转的。
结论
选 D： 这是最像 Cent. Hudson 的答法。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：题干说这些电话“occasionally misleading”，那州是不是就能一把全禁？

但考试真正问的是：这批电话是不是已经掉进“完全不受保护”的坑里；如果不是，就要按商业言论的中度审查来走。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

同样道理，本题看的是州政府能不能用substantial interest加narrow tailoring把限制站住，不是看它有没有一个听起来很烦人的社会问题。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干 30 天内禁拨 仍是在管受保护商业言论；州方只要证明隐私保护和医疗监管是重大利益，且限制方式贴着目标走，就能成立。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把 some speech 当成整类失保，忽略题干并没说这些电话全是虚假。

❌ 法律适用 | 审查等级误判

✕ B: 直接搬出rationally related，把受保护商业言论的中度审查偷换成低标准。

❌ 事实误判 | 内容中立偷换

✕ C: 把按内容禁电话说成time, place, and manner，其实它就是冲着说什么来的。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是不是受保护商业言论，再套 Cent. Hudson 的“重大利益 + 窄限”两步。

考场速记

记住一句话：商业言论（commercial speech）不是“看到烦就能禁”，先问它是不是虚假或违法；不是的话，就看州政府能不能同时证明substantial interest和narrowly tailored。

再记口诀：“先看保护，再看两步；想到 Cent. Hudson，别把中度审查说成理性基础审查。”

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state's department of education routinely accredits public and private schools, licenses their teachers, sets strict curriculum guidelines, and provides funds for buses and secular extracurricular activities. A private high school in the state receives all of these benefits and enforces a strict "whites only" admissions policy.
A group of parents whose children were denied admission to the private school solely because they are minorities brought suit in federal court. The parents sought to enjoin the private school from continuing its admissions policy on the ground that it violates the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. The private school's sole defense is that it is not bound by this constitutional provision.
What is the parents' strongest argument that the private school must comply with the equal protection clause?

choices.A: Education is a traditional public function.
choices.B: Racial segregation is not allowed in any school.
choices.C: The private school employs teachers licensed by the state.
choices.D: The private school is subject to pervasive state regulation and support.

questions.explanation:
State-action doctrine
Traditional government function
  • Private actor performs traditional & exclusive government function (eg, running elections)
Significant government involvement
  • Government & private actor have mutually beneficial relationship (eg, joint activity or venture)
  • Government creates nexus by affirmatively facilitating or authorizing private action (eg, police officer acting under color of law)
  • Government is pervasively intertwined in private entity's management or control

Constitutional claims must typically be asserted against government entities—not private actors.* But under the state-action doctrine, a private actor can be treated as a government entity and similarly bound by the Constitution when the government is pervasively intertwined in the control or management of the private actor.

Here, the parents sought to enjoin the private school from continuing its racially segregated admissions policy on the ground that it violates the Fourteenth Amendment equal protection clause. Therefore, the strongest argument that the private school must comply with this clause is that the school is subject to pervasive state regulation and support—e.g., through state accreditation, teacher licensing, curriculum guidelines, funding for buses and secular extracurricular activities.

*The Thirteenth Amendment's prohibition against slavery is the only constitutional provision that directly applies to private conduct.

(Choice A) Private entities can be treated as state actors if they perform a function that has traditionally and exclusively been performed by the state. Although education is a public function, it has long been undertaken by private entities—not just the state. Therefore, the private school will not be treated as a state actor on this basis.

(Choice B) States are constitutionally obligated to eliminate segregation in all public schools within their borders. However, racial segregation is allowed in private schools that do not have significant government involvement.

(Choice C) The fact that the private school employs state-licensed teachers does not, by itself, require the school to comply with the equal protection clause. That is because the Supreme Court held in Moose Lodge No. 107 v. Irvis that issuing a license—without more—does not amount to significant government involvement.

📌 Educational Objective

The Constitution generally applies to government (not private) entities. But under the state-action doctrine, a private entity will be bound by the Constitution when the government is so pervasively intertwined in its control or management that the private entity is essentially a government actor.

📚 References
  • Brentwood Acad. v. Tenn. Secondary Sch. Athletic Ass'n, 531 U.S. 288, 298–302 (2001) (recognizing that a private association's regulatory activity amounted to state action due to the state's pervasive entwinement).
  • Moose Lodge No. 107 v. Irvis, 407 U.S. 163, 176–77 (1972) (explaining that mere licensure does not amount to significant government involvement).
questions.zh-question:
某州教育部门定期认证公立和私立学校，为其教师颁发执照，制定严格的课程指南，并为校车和世俗课外活动提供资金。

该州的一所私立高中享有所有这些福利，并执行严格的“仅限白人”的招生政策。

一群家长因其子女仅仅因为是少数族裔而被该私立学校拒绝录取，向联邦法院提起诉讼。这些家长以该私立学校的招生政策违反了Fourteenth Amendment（第十四修正案）的平等保护条款为由，请求法院颁布禁令，禁止该校继续执行其招生政策。该私立学校的唯一辩护理由是它不受此宪法条款的约束。

家长们主张该私立学校必须遵守平等保护条款的最有力论据是什么？

zh-choices.A: 教育是一项传统的公共职能。
zh-choices.B: 任何学校都不允许实行种族隔离。
zh-choices.C: 该私立学校雇用了持有州执照的教师。
zh-choices.D: 该私立学校受到州政府的普遍性监管和支持。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Individual Rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：私立学校在政府“过度缠绕”到管理和控制时，能不能被当成国家行为人（state actor），从而受平等保护条款（equal protection clause）约束。

三秒认题路径：

私校歧视 → 先问私主体 → 看州参与 → 缠得够深 → 算国家行为

核心法律规则

宪法通常只管政府，不直接管私人；所以先问这所学校是不是国家行为人（state actor），考场意思：如果还只是普通私校，平等保护条款（equal protection clause）一般打不到它。

真正能把私人“拉进”宪法的，是政府对私人机构的过度缠绕（pervasive entwinement），考场意思：政府不只是给个牌照，而是已经深度介入它的管理、控制、日常运作。

所以这题要抓的是：州教育部门给这所学校做认证、给教师发执照、定课程、还提供校车和课外活动经费，已经不是“碰一下”而是“管进去了”。

核心判例： Brentwood Acad. v. Tenn. Secondary Sch. Athletic Ass'n —— 说明政府与私主体“缠得太深”时，私主体也会被当成国家行为人。

思维导图

先问：这所私校能不能被当成国家行为人？
NO 只是普通私立学校 → 宪法一般不直接管。
但本题有吗 州认证、教师执照、课程规则、经费支持 → 政府深度介入。
卡死点：不是单纯发牌照，而是pervasive entwinement，所以可直接套equal protection。
YES 私校被当成国家行为人 → 不能靠“我只是私人”逃掉。
对照陷阱：Moose Lodge 只说“发执照而已”不够；本题是“监管 + 支持 + 管理”一起上。
终点：选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这题只是“私校歧视黑人”，那就直接想到公立学校那套平等保护，或以为“州给教师发执照”已经足够。

但考试真正问的是：这家私校有没有被州政府管到足以变成state actor。

司法考试看的是「政府程序上能不能把它算进来」，而不是「私校歧视看起来有多坏」。

所以“发执照”本身不够，真正有用的是州对学校认证、课程、人员和资金的整套控制。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干写明州教育部门对这所私校有认证、教师执照、课程规则、经费支持，这就是政府与私校的深度缠绕，所以它要受equal protection约束。

❌ 概念混淆 | 公私功能混用

✕ A: 把“教育”硬说成州独占功能，但私校长期也办教育。

❌ 法律适用 | 公校规则套错

✕ B: 这是把公立学校的禁令直接搬到私校上。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看发证忽略控制

✕ C: 只盯着licensed teachers，但单纯发执照不够。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判私主体能否被拉成国家行为人，再看州是不是已经深度介入管理。

考场速记

记住这句：private actor + pervasive entwinement = state action。碰到私校、公会、协会这类题，先别急着背结论，先问政府是不是已经管到它像个公家机构。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A city school board issued a rule authorizing public school principals to punish, after a hearing, students who violate the board's student behavior code. According to the rule, violators of the behavior code may be punished in a variety of ways, including being required to sit in designated school-confinement rooms during all school hours, with their hands clasped in front of them, for a period of up to 15 school days.
A fifth-grade student in a city elementary school was charged with placing chewed bubble gum on a classmate's chair, a violation of the student behavior code. He had never violated the code before and was otherwise an attentive and well-behaved student. After a hearing on the charges, the student's principal determined that the student had violated the behavior code in the manner charged and ordered the student to spend the next 15 school days in the school-confinement room with his hands clasped in front of him.
The student's parents file suit in federal court challenging, solely on constitutional grounds, the principal's action in ordering the student to spend the next 15 school days in the school-confinement room with his hands clasped in front of him.
Which of the following arguments would be most helpful to the student's parents in this suit?

choices.A: Because application of the school board rule in this case denies the student freedom of movement and subjects him to bodily restraint in a manner grossly disproportionate to his offense and circumstances, it violates the due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.B: Because the school board rule is enforced initially by administrative rather than judicial proceedings, it constitutes a prohibited bill of attainder.
choices.C: Because the school board rule is substantially overbroad in relation to any legitimate purpose, it constitutes a facial violation of the equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment.
choices.D: Because the school board rule limits the freedom of movement of students and subjects them to bodily restraint, it denies them a privilege and immunity of citizenship guaranteed them by Article IV, Section 2.

questions.explanation:
Fourteenth Amendment protections
Clause Applicability
Equal protection Discriminatory treatment of similarly situated people
Due process Substantive – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate justification
Procedural – deprivation of life, liberty, or property without adequate process
Privileges or immunities* Interference with rights of national citizenship
*Rarely a correct answer.

Substantive due process prohibits the government from depriving persons of life, liberty, or property (eg, freedom of movement) without adequate justification. At a minimum, due process requires that any such government action be rationally related to a legitimate government interest (ie, rational basis review). A government action that is grossly disproportionate to a person's offense or circumstances cannot satisfy this standard of review.

Here, the principal applied a school board rule and ordered the student to spend 15 days in confinement after he placed gum on a classmate's chair. But the student had never violated the behavior code before and was otherwise attentive and well-behaved. As a result, the parents' best argument is that the application of the school board rule violates due process because it subjects the student to bodily restraint in a manner grossly disproportionate to his offense and circumstances.

(Choice B) State and federal governments are prohibited from passing bills of attainder—ie, legislative acts that punish a specific person or group without a judicial trial. But since this school board rule allows punishment of any student who violates the behavior code—not just a specific student or group—it is not a bill of attainder.

(Choice C) A rule is facially invalid (eg, substantially overbroad) if no application of the rule is constitutional. But the school board rule is not a facial violation of the equal protection clause since it applies equally to all students.

(Choice D) The Article IV privileges and immunities clause prohibits states from discriminating against out-of-state residents by denying them a right of state citizenship. This clause does not apply here since the student is a resident of the school district—not an out-of-state resident.

📌 Educational Objective

Substantive due process prohibits government deprivations of life, liberty, or property that are not rationally related to a legitimate government interest—eg, grossly disproportionate punishments.

📚 References
  • Cooper Indus. v. Leatherman Tool Grp., 532 U.S. 424, 433–35 (2001) (explaining that the due process clause prohibits government punishments that are "grossly disproportional" to the offense).
questions.zh-question:
一个市教育委员会颁布了一项规则，授权公立学校校长在举行听证会后，惩罚违反该委员会学生行为准则的学生。根据该规则，违反行为准则者可能受到多种方式的惩罚，包括被要求在所有上课时间内坐在指定的学校禁闭室里，双手在身前紧握，时间最长可达15个上学日。

该市一所小学的五年级学生被指控将嚼过的泡泡糖放在同学的椅子上，这违反了学生行为准则。他以前从未违反过该准则，并且在其他方面是一个专注且行为良好的学生。在对指控举行听证会后，该学生的校长认定该学生确实以上述方式违反了行为准则，并命令该学生在接下来的15个上学日里，在学校禁闭室中双手紧握度过。

该学生的父母向联邦法院提起诉讼，仅以宪法为由，质疑校长命令该学生在接下来的15个上学日里在学校禁闭室中双手紧握度过的行为。

在此诉讼中，以下哪项论点对该学生的父母最有帮助？

zh-choices.A: 因为在本案中适用学校委员会的规则剥夺了学生的行动自由，并以一种与其过错和情节严重不成比例的方式对其施加身体约束，这违反了Fourteenth Amendment的正当程序条款。
zh-choices.B: 因为学校委员会的规则最初是通过行政程序而非司法程序来执行的，所以它构成了被禁止的剥夺公权法案（bill of attainder）。
zh-choices.C: 因为学校委员会的规则相对于任何合法目的而言都过于宽泛，所以它构成了对Fourteenth Amendment的平等保护条款的表面违宪。
zh-choices.D: 因为学校委员会的规则限制了学生的行动自由并对他们施加身体约束，所以它剥夺了Article IV, Section 2所保障的公民特权和豁免权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Miscellaneous

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：学校纪律处分是否因对学生限制过重而触发第十四修正案的实质性正当程序（substantive due process）。

三秒认题路径：

校规处分 → 关拘束室 → 15天 → 过重惩罚 → 实质性正当程序

核心法律规则

实质性正当程序（substantive due process）禁止政府在没有足够正当理由下剥夺生命、自由或财产，自由（liberty）包括行动自由和身体不受不当拘束。考场意思：不是问学校有没有规矩，而是问这次处罚是不是太重、重到和违纪行为不成比例。

rational basis review 只是最低门槛；如果政府动作对错误或情节grossly disproportionate，就过不了。考试上你只要抓住“一个小错误换来长时间身体拘束”，就会想到正当程序问题。

核心判例：Cooper Indus. v. Leatherman Tool Grp. —— 说明政府惩罚若对行为“grossly disproportional”，就可能违反正当程序。

思维导图

题目先看：这是不是在问“处罚太重”导致的宪法问题？
Step 1：校规是一般规则，不是专门点名某个学生的立法惩罚。
Step 2：处分内容是15天拘束室 + 双手交叠，属于对liberty 的直接限制。
Step 3：看比例：一次放口香糖到椅子上，却给出长时间身体拘束，显得grossly disproportionate → 正当程序不过关
结论：父母最有力的说法是：这次适用校规违反第十四修正案的substantive due process。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：校规是统一适用于所有学生的，所以好像只能争“平等保护（equal protection）”。

但考试真正问的是：这次处分本身是否对这个学生过度，是否侵犯了他的自由而缺乏足够正当理由。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里真正的杀招不是“规则写得整不整齐”，而是“惩罚重不重、有没有过度”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干 15 days in confinement 还要双手交叠，已经是在直接限制自由；对一次轻微违纪来说，这种处罚明显过重，所以应走实质性正当程序。

❌ 法律适用 | 立法惩罚误判

✕ B: 把一般校规当成bill of attainder，但它不是点名惩罚特定人。

❌ 概念混淆 | 平权审查误判

✕ C: 看到overbroad 就乱套到平等保护，其实它平等适用于所有学生。

❌ 事实误判 | 外州身份偷换

✕ D: 把privileges and immunities 硬套进来，但这学生不是外州居民。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓处分强度，再看是否明显失衡；别被“有校规”带跑去做平权或立法惩罚判断。

考场速记

记住一句：实质性正当程序（substantive due process）看的是“处罚有没有过重到不合理”。一旦看到“轻微违纪 + 长时间拘束/身体限制”，先想比例失衡，而不是先找别的宪法标签。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify the applicable constitutional protection

reason.en: Their conduct constitutes government action subject to constitutional limits.
reason.zh: 其行为属于受宪法限制的政府行为。

reason.en: The hearing makes procedural due process a weaker challenge than substantive due process.
reason.zh: 已举行听证，使程序性正当程序主张弱于实体性正当程序主张。

keywords.text: with their hands clasped in front of them

reason.en: This restraint implicates the student's liberty and freedom of movement.
reason.zh: 该约束涉及学生的人身自由与行动自由。

reason.en: The lengthy duration supports the argument that the punishment is grossly disproportionate.
reason.zh: 较长的期限支持处罚严重不成比例的主张。

keywords.text: placing chewed bubble gum on a classmate's chair

reason.en: The minor offense provides the baseline for evaluating proportionality.
reason.zh: 该轻微行为是评估处罚比例性的基准。

keywords.text: had never violated the code before

reason.en: The student's clean record makes the maximum punishment less justifiable.
reason.zh: 学生无违纪前科，使最高处罚更难获得正当化。

reason.en: The parents must identify the constitutional provision best suited to the facts.
reason.zh: 家长必须确定最适用于本案事实的宪法条款。

reason.en: Freedom of movement is a liberty interest protected by substantive due process.
reason.zh: 行动自由是实体性正当程序所保护的自由利益。

A.text: grossly disproportionate to his offense and circumstances

reason.en: Gross disproportionality shows that the restraint lacks adequate governmental justification.
reason.zh: 严重不成比例表明该约束缺乏充分的政府正当理由。

A.text: due process clause of the Fourteenth Amendment

label.zh: 第十四修正案实体性正当程序保护

reason.en: This is the constitutional provision applicable to an unjustified deprivation of liberty.
reason.zh: 该宪法条款适用于缺乏正当理由的自由剥夺。

reason.en: A nonjudicial proceeding alone does not make a generally applicable rule a bill of attainder.
reason.zh: 仅采用非司法程序并不会使普遍适用的规则成为剥夺公权法案。

reason.en: The doctrine requires legislation targeting an identifiable person or group, which is absent here.
reason.zh: 该原则要求立法针对可识别的个人或群体，而本案并不存在这一条件。

reason.en: The facts support an as-applied proportionality challenge, not facial invalidity.
reason.zh: 事实支持具体适用中的比例性挑战，而非表面无效主张。

reason.en: The parents challenge this particular punishment, and constitutional applications of the rule remain possible.
reason.zh: 家长挑战的是本次具体处罚，且该规则仍可能存在合宪适用。

C.text: equal protection clause of the Fourteenth Amendment

label.zh: 第十四修正案平等保护条款

reason.en: No discriminatory classification or unequal treatment of similarly situated students is alleged.
reason.zh: 本案未主张存在歧视性分类或对处境相同学生的不平等待遇。

reason.en: This protection concerns state discrimination against citizens of other states, not school discipline.
reason.zh: 该保护针对州对外州公民的歧视，而非学校纪律处分。

label.en: Article IV Privileges and Immunities Clause
label.zh: 宪法第四条特权与豁免条款

reason.en: The clause is inapplicable because the facts involve no discrimination against an out-of-state citizen.
reason.zh: 事实不涉及对外州公民的歧视，因此该条款不适用。

highlights.text: placing chewed bubble gum on a classmate's chair

reason.en: The trivial nature of the offense is essential to evaluating whether the punishment is grossly disproportionate.
reason.zh: 该行为的轻微性质是判断处罚是否严重不成比例的关键。

highlights.text: He had never violated the code before and was otherwise an attentive and well-behaved student.

reason.en: These mitigating facts weaken any justification for imposing the maximum confinement.
reason.zh: 这些减轻因素削弱了施加最长禁闭处罚的正当性。

highlights.text: the next 15 school days in the school-confinement room with his hands clasped in front of him

reason.en: The duration and bodily restraint establish a serious deprivation of liberty.
reason.zh: 处罚期限与身体约束构成严重的自由剥夺。

highlights.text: solely on constitutional grounds

reason.en: This limitation requires selecting the constitutional doctrine that directly addresses the unjustified restraint.
reason.zh: 这一限制要求选择直接规制无正当理由身体约束的宪法原则。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A state generally provides funding for the medical care of its residents who cannot afford such care. State law, however, prohibits use of this state funding for surgery for any person who has resided in the state for less than one year, except in emergency situations.
A woman moved to the state two months ago seeking permanent employment. Her physician recommends non-emergency surgery to treat a medical condition. The surgery would qualify for state funding if the woman had resided in the state for a year. The woman has sued to invalidate the state law that prohibits state funding of her surgery.
Should the woman prevail in her action?

choices.A: No, because the law reasonably conserves the state's limited resources.
choices.B: No, because the law reasonably prevents the expenditure of state funds on transient nonresidents.
choices.C: Yes, because the law burdens the woman's fundamental right to health care.
choices.D: Yes, because the law burdens the woman's fundamental right to travel.

questions.explanation:
A woman who recently moved to the state was denied access to state funding for a surgery due to a durational residency requirement. Laws with this requirement are generally reviewed under the equal protection clause since they treat two classes of persons differently—those who have resided in the state for a designated period and those who have not. And since these laws substantially burden the fundamental right to travel by discouraging persons from moving into the state, they are subject to strict scrutiny and almost always held unconstitutional. Therefore, the woman should prevail in her action to invalidate the law.

(Choices A & B) A law's ability to reasonably achieve a legitimate state interest (eg, conservation of state resources or funds) would validate the law under the rational basis test. But this test only applies when a law does not substantially impact a fundamental right or suspect class (which triggers strict scrutiny) or a quasi-suspect class (which triggers intermediate scrutiny).

(Choice C) There is no fundamental right to health care, so the law will not be invalidated on this basis.

📌 Educational Objective

Since durational residency requirements burden the fundamental right to travel, they are strictly scrutinized and almost always held unconstitutional under the equal protection clause.

📚 References
  • Shapiro v. Thompson, 394 U.S. 618, 627 (1969) (invalidating durational residency requirement under strict scrutiny equal protection analysis).
questions.zh-question:
一个州通常为其无力负担医疗费用的居民提供医疗保健资金。然而，州法律禁止将此州资金用于为在该州居住不满一年的任何人提供手术，紧急情况除外。

一名女性两个月前搬到该州寻求永久性工作。她的医生建议进行非紧急手术来治疗一种疾病。如果该女性在该州居住满一年，该手术将有资格获得州政府的资助。该女性已提起诉讼，要求宣告禁止州政府资助其手术的州法律无效。

该女性的诉讼应该会胜诉吗？

zh-choices.A: 不会，因为该法律合理地保护了该州有限的资源。
zh-choices.B: 不会，因为该法律合理地防止了州政府资金被用于临时的非居民。
zh-choices.C: 会，因为该法律给该女性的基本医疗保健权带来了负担。
zh-choices.D: 会，因为该法律给该女性的基本旅行权带来了负担。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Individual Rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府用“一年居住期”卡住医疗补助，是否侵犯了迁徙自由（fundamental right to travel），所以要不要按严格审查（strict scrutiny）直接打掉。

三秒认题路径：

一年居住期 → 州福利限制 → 迁徙自由 → 严格审查 → D

核心法律规则

居住期限要求（durational residency requirement）如果让新搬来的人比老居民少拿福利，就在等着被按平等保护条款（Equal Protection Clause）审查。这里真正被压到的是迁徙自由（right to travel），考场意思：州不能靠“你住不满一年就别想拿”来吓退外来者。

这类规定通常触发严格审查（strict scrutiny），州必须证明它是为迫切州利益（compelling state interest）所必需，而且手段最窄。像节省财政开支这种理由，通常不够硬。

核心判例： Shapiro v. Thompson —— 一年居住期限制公共福利，因压迫迁徙自由而被严格审查并通常判违宪。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决吗？
NO州法把“住满一年”设成拿医疗费的门槛。
再问它有没有在赶人？
有：它让新搬来的人先别住，直接碰到迁徙自由。
关卡durational residency requirement → right to travel → strict scrutiny
州要证明：限制necessary，而且为了compelling state interest。
省钱、守财政、赶“暂住者”都不够把它救回来。
终点结论：这条法大概率被打掉，所以选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州只是想省钱、别把有限资金花给“刚来的人”。

但考试真正问的是：它是不是用居住期限去挡新居民拿福利，进而碰到right to travel。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

这题不是在问“州有没有合理理财”，而是在问“它能不能用住满一年当门槛去区别对待新迁入者”。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的一年居住期就是典型的 durational residency requirement，会压到迁徙自由，所以要用严格审查，州很难赢。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 误把conserves the state's当成足够理由，忽略了严格审查。

❌ 事实误判 | 暂住标签偷换

✕ B: 把“没住满一年”偷换成可随便排斥transient nonresidents，但题目是新居民而非外州人。

❌ 法律适用 | 健康权套错题

✕ C: 误以为有fundamental right to health care，其实没有这个权利。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“居住期限”这类门槛，再直接切到迁徙自由与严格审查。

考场速记

记住：durational residency requirement 一旦挡到福利，先想 right to travel，再想 strict scrutiny。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 主要记程序例外；但本题记的是“居住门槛碰到迁徙自由，通常过不了”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Identify strict scrutiny for residency requirements

keywords.text: prohibits use of this state funding

reason.en: Identifies the government benefit withheld from recent residents.
reason.zh: 表明州政府拒绝向新近居民提供的公共福利。

keywords.text: resided in the state for less than one year

reason.en: This residency classification burdens the fundamental right to interstate travel.
reason.zh: 该居住期限分类限制了州际迁徙的基本权利。

reason.en: Limits the funding prohibition but does not apply to the recommended surgery.
reason.zh: 该例外限制资金禁令的范围，但不适用于所建议的手术。

keywords.text: moved to the state two months ago

reason.en: Shows that the woman is a new resident affected by the one-year waiting period.
reason.zh: 表明该女子属于受一年等待期影响的新居民。

reason.en: Undermines any characterization of the woman as a transient nonresident.
reason.zh: 否定了将该女子视为临时非居民的说法。

label.zh: 不属于紧急例外的医疗

reason.en: Confirms that the statutory emergency exception cannot provide funding.
reason.zh: 确认法定紧急情况例外不能为该手术提供资金。

keywords.text: sued to invalidate the state law

reason.en: Frames the issue as whether the residency restriction is unconstitutional.
reason.zh: 将争点界定为该居住限制是否违宪。

reason.en: Uses rational-basis reasoning even though a fundamental right triggers strict scrutiny.
reason.zh: 在基本权利触发严格审查时错误使用合理基础审查。

reason.en: Conserving funds ordinarily cannot justify penalizing recent interstate migrants.
reason.zh: 节约资金通常不足以证明对近期州际迁居者的不利待遇合理。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
To encourage the growth of its population, a state established a program that awarded $1,000 to the parents of each child born within the state, provided that at the time of the child's birth the mother and father of the newborn were citizens of the United States.
A married couple, noncitizens who are permanent residents of the United States, have resided in the state for three years. When their first child was born two months ago, they applied for and were denied the $1,000 award by state officials on the sole ground that they are not citizens of the United States. The couple filed suit in federal court contending that their exclusion from the award program was unconstitutional. Assume no federal statute addresses this question.
In this case, how should the court rule as to the constitutionality of the state's exclusion of noncitizens from the award program?

choices.A: The exclusion is constitutional, because the state has a legitimate interest in encouraging the growth of its population, and a rational legislature could believe that families in which both parents are United States citizens are more likely to stay in the state and contribute to its future prosperity than those in which one or both of the parents are noncitizens.
choices.B: The exclusion is constitutional, because the Tenth Amendment reserves to the states plenary authority over the spending of state funds.
choices.C: The exclusion is unconstitutional, because state classifications based on citizenship are impermissible unless explicitly authorized by an act of Congress.
choices.D: The exclusion is unconstitutional, because strict scrutiny governs judicial review of such state classifications based on citizenship, and the state cannot demonstrate that this classification is necessary to advance a compelling state interest.

questions.explanation:
Discriminatory state action can be challenged on Fourteenth Amendment equal protection grounds. When such action discriminates against a suspect class or substantially impacts a fundamental right, it must survive strict scrutiny—the most stringent standard of review. This requires the state to prove that its action is necessary to advance a compelling state interest. And since this is a nearly impossible standard to meet, state actions subject to strict scrutiny are almost always held unconstitutional.

Here, the state program discriminates against parents who are resident noncitizens by denying them the $1,000 award given to other parents of newborns. Since citizenship is a suspect class, strict scrutiny applies. And since the state's interest in promoting population growth could be achieved without excluding resident noncitizens from its award program, the state cannot demonstrate that its actions were necessary to advance a compelling state interest. As a result, the court should find the state's exclusion of noncitizens from the award program unconstitutional.

(Choice A) Under the rational basis test (the least stringent standard of review), government actions are constitutional as long as they are rationally related to a legitimate state interest. But this test only applies when the government action does not impact a quasi-suspect class, suspect class, or fundamental right.

(Choice B) The Tenth Amendment gives the states any powers not given to the federal government. But states must comply with other constitutional provisions like the equal protection clause when exercising those powers.

(Choice C) Congress cannot authorize state classifications based on citizenship. Such classifications must survive strict judicial scrutiny instead.

📌 Educational Objective

State actions that discriminate against a suspect class or substantially impact a fundamental right are subject to strict scrutiny. Under this most stringent standard of review, such actions are unconstitutional unless the state can prove that they are necessary to advance a compelling state interest.

📚 References
  • Nyquist v. Mauclet, 432 U.S. 1, 7 (1977) (explaining that state classifications based on citizenship are inherently suspect and subject to strict scrutiny).

在此案中，法院应如何裁定该州将外国人排除在奖励计划之外的做法是否合宪？

zh-choices.A: 该排除合宪，因为该州在鼓励其人口增长方面拥有合法利益，一个理性的立法机构可能会认为，父母双方都是美国公民的家庭比父母一方或双方是外国人的家庭更有可能留在该州，并为其未来的繁荣做出贡献。
zh-choices.B: 该排除合宪，因为 Tenth Amendment 将州资金支出的完全权力保留给各州。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Suspect classifications

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州政府按公民身份（citizenship）排除非公民，是否要用严格审查（strict scrutiny）看合宪性。

三秒认题路径：

非公民 → 州排除 → 可疑分类 → 严格审查 → 不能过

核心法律规则

只记这条就够做题

州政府一旦按公民身份（citizenship）区别对待，考试上先把它当成可疑分类（suspect classification）；考场意思：不是普通“合理就行”，而是直接进最严的审查档位。

进入严格审查（strict scrutiny）后，州必须证明这个排除措施对实现一个压倒性州利益（compelling state interest）是necessary；考场意思：能不能不用歧视也达到目标，才是关键。

这题里州想提高人口，完全可以用不排除非公民的方式做，所以它过不了这个门槛，结论就是违宪。

核心判例： Nyquist v. Mauclet — 州的公民身份分类本身就很危险，通常要按严格审查处理。

思维导图

州按“是不是美国公民”来发放奖金？
是先看是不是可疑分类（suspect classification）。
规则州的公民身份分类 → 严格审查（strict scrutiny）。
再问州能否证明：非这样排除就达不到压倒性州利益（compelling state interest）？
卡死点：这题的利益不是“必须排除非公民才行”，所以第三步过不了。
结论不能立刻把非公民踢出奖金计划，答案选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：州只是想让人口增长，rational basis 也许就够了。

但考试真正问的是：这是公民身份（citizenship）歧视，不是普通经济政策，所以要直接上严格审查（strict scrutiny）。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的state excludes noncitizens直接触发可疑分类（suspect classification），所以要用严格审查；州只是在追求人口增长，做不到“非排除不可”。

❌ 概念混淆 | 合理审查误判

✕ A: 把公民身份歧视偷换成普通政策，错用了rational basis。

❌ 法律适用 | 第十修正案误判

✕ B: 只看到州出钱，就忘了州花钱也要受平等保护约束。

❌ 事实误判 | 国会授权偷换

✕ C: 题干根本没给Congress授权这个分类，直接把例外当规则。

这题建议用什么方法？

先认分类，再锁审查标准：公民身份歧视先跳到严格审查，别被“州想做好事”带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：公民身份（citizenship）上州法，先想严格审查（strict scrutiny）；能不用歧视也能达成目标，就别想过关。

这题可顺手记：Nyquist v. Mauclet。看到州按公民身份筛人，先问“是不是可疑分类”，再问“有没有非排除不可”。

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
To improve the quality of rental housing within its boundaries, a city proposed an ordinance requiring all new and existing rental-housing units to provide at least one full bathroom for each bedroom, plumbing and electrical hookups for a washer and dryer, and a covered parking space.
A majority of the owners of existing rental housing in the city opposed the ordinance. They argued that it would dramatically decrease the number of low-income rental-housing units because owners would be unable to raise rents enough to recoup the investment required to comply. Without denying these contentions, the city enacted the ordinance. A plaintiff who owns low-income rental housing has sued the city, claiming only that the ordinance is unconstitutional on its face.
Which of the following best states the burden of persuasion in this action?

choices.A: The city must demonstrate that the ordinance is necessary to serve a compelling state interest, because it adversely affects the fundamental right of rental-housing owners to use their property in the manner they deem most economically efficient.
choices.B: The city must demonstrate that the ordinance is necessary to serve a compelling state interest, because it will have a substantial and disproportionate negative impact on low-income persons.
choices.C: The plaintiff must demonstrate that the ordinance is not substantially related to an important state interest, because it requires some owners of rental housing to invest money that they will not be able to recoup from increased rents.
choices.D: The plaintiff must demonstrate that there is no rational relationship between the ordinance and any legitimate state interest, because the ordinance regulates economic activity of a type normally presumed to be within state regulatory authority.

questions.explanation:
All state and local laws must comply with the Fourteenth Amendment, including the substantive due process and equal protection clauses. The substantive due process clause applies when a law impacts all persons, while the equal protection clause applies when a law impacts a particular class of persons. And under either clause, the challenged law must survive the appropriate level of scrutiny:

  • rational basis scrutiny (default test) – requires the challenger to show that the law is not rationally related to any legitimate state interest
  • intermediate scrutiny (quasi-suspect class) – requires the state to show that the law is substantially related to an important state interest or
  • strict scrutiny (suspect class or fundamental right) – requires the state to show that the law is necessary to serve a compelling state interest.

Here, the city ordinance requires all rental-housing units to include certain amenities. Although this may have a substantial and disproportionate negative impact on low-income persons, wealth-based classifications are not a suspect or quasi-suspect class (Choice B). And rental-housing owners do not have a fundamental right to use their property in any manner (Choice A). Instead, the ordinance regulates the type of economic activity normally presumed to be within a state's authority. Therefore, the plaintiff has the burden to satisfy rational basis scrutiny.

(Choice C) The city would have to show that the ordinance is substantially related to an important government interest had the ordinance substantially impacted a quasi-suspect class.

📌 Educational Objective

Under the Fourteenth Amendment due process and equal protection clauses, most state and local laws are subject to rational basis review. This standard requires the challenger to demonstrate that the law has no rational relation to any legitimate state interest.

📚 References
  • Pennell v. San Jose, 485 U.S. 1, 13–14 (1988) (applying rational basis scrutiny to a price-control ordinance since it does not impact a protected class or a fundamental right).
questions.zh-question:
为了提高其管辖范围内的租赁住房质量，某市提出一项法令，要求所有新的和现有的租赁住房单元为每间卧室至少提供一间设施齐全的浴室，为洗衣机和烘干机提供水电接口，以及一个带顶棚的停车位。

该市现有租赁住房的大多数业主反对该法令。他们认为，这将导致低收入租赁住房单元的数量急剧减少，因为业主将无法通过提高租金来收回为遵守法令所需进行的投资。在没有否认这些论点的情况下，该市颁布了该法令。一名拥有低收入租赁住房的原告已起诉该市，仅声称该法令本身违宪。

下列哪项最能说明本诉讼中的说服责任？

zh-choices.A: 该市必须证明该法令对于服务于迫切的国家利益是必要的，因为它对租赁住房业主以其认为最经济有效的方式使用其财产的基本权利产生了不利影响。
zh-choices.B: 该市必须证明该法令对于服务于迫切的国家利益是必要的，因为它将对低收入人群产生重大且不成比例的负面影响。
zh-choices.C: 原告必须证明该法令与重要的国家利益没有实质性关系，因为它要求一些租赁住房业主投入他们无法通过提高租金来收回的资金。
zh-choices.D: 原告必须证明该法令与任何合法的国家利益之间没有合理关系，因为该法令规范的是通常被推定为属于州监管权力范围内的经济活动。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - Individual Rights

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：这类面向所有租赁住房的城市住房规范，默认走 理性基础审查（rational basis review），而不是严格审查。

三秒认题路径：

经济管制 → 非嫌疑分类 → 无基本权利 → 理性基础 → 由挑战者举证

核心法律规则

先看审查强度，再看谁负担举证

州和地方政府的法规要过第十四修正案审查；如果不是 嫌疑分类（suspect class） 或 基本权利（fundamental right），考试默认走 理性基础审查（rational basis review），也就是先看“有没有合理联系”。

这里的 住房装修与经济管制（economic regulation） 只是要求出租房增加设施，不会因为它影响低收入人群，就自动升级到严格审查。财富分层（wealth-based classification） 不是嫌疑分类，所以不会把举证责任翻到政府身上。

因此，本题要问的是：原告能不能证明这条规定 has no rational relationship to any legitimate state interest。答案是不能由城市先证明“必要性”；默认仍是挑战者先扛这道门槛。

核心判例： Pennell v. San Jose — 住房价格与租赁管制若不碰嫌疑分类或基本权利，仍按理性基础审查处理。

思维导图

先问：这条城市出租房条例，碰到的是 基本权利 或 嫌疑分类 吗？
NO只是要求每间出租房加浴室、洗衣烘干接口、车位，属于 经济管制。
NO不会自动升级到 strict scrutiny；低收入受影响，也不是嫌疑分类。
进入默认门槛 rational basis review：原告要证明没有任何合理关系。
结论城市只要有合法目的即可，故 选 D。
考场提示看见“面向所有租赁住房”“成本高”“回本困难”，先别被同情心带跑，先锁定审查强度。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这条规定让低收入租客更难找到房子，听起来很不公平，所以应该用严格审查。

但考试真正问的是：它有没有碰到 嫌疑分类 或 基本权利；低收入受冲击只是结果难看，不会自己把审查强度拉高。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干是统一适用于出租住房的 经济性住房条例，既不碰嫌疑分类，也不碰基本权利，所以原告要先证明“完全不合理”。

❌ 概念混淆 | 基本权利误判

✕ A: 把房东的 most economically efficient 当成基本权利了。

❌ 事实误判 | 贫困分类误判

✕ B: 低收入受影响，不等于题目承认了可疑分类。

❌ 法律适用 | 中间审查错套

✕ C: 把 substantially related 硬套进来，但本题没有 quasi-suspect class。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定审查强度，再决定举证责任；只要没碰嫌疑分类或基本权利，就先想理性基础审查。

考场速记

记住：经济管制（economic regulation） 默认走 理性基础审查（rational basis review），不要看到“对低收入人群很不友好”就自动升级。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是上诉例外记忆句；但这题不是上诉题，核心仍是“非嫌疑、非基本权利，就先让挑战者证明不合理”。

keywords.text: all new and existing rental-housing units

A.text: necessary to serve a compelling state interest

C.text: not substantially related to an important state interest

reason.en: This invokes intermediate scrutiny and incorrectly places its burden on the plaintiff.
reason.zh: 该表述适用中度审查，却错误地将其责任置于原告。

reason.en: Economic loss does not by itself trigger heightened constitutional scrutiny.

label.zh: 合理基础审查中的原告责任

reason.en: Under rational basis review, the challenger must negate a rational relationship.

reason.en: A legitimate state interest is sufficient under rational basis review.
reason.zh: 在合理基础审查下，合法的州利益即已足够。

reason.en: Ordinary economic regulation is presumptively reviewed under rational basis scrutiny.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.question:
A county school board has adopted a program that will hire teachers to teach English to elementary school students whose primary language is not English. The teachers will be employed by the school board and assigned to all public and private schools within the county. Most of the private schools in the county are faith-based, so the program has adopted procedures to ensure that the teachers are not involved in religious instruction. The number of teachers allocated to each school will be based solely on the number of nonnative English-speakers enrolled at the school.
Does the program likely violate the establishment clause of the First Amendment?

choices.A: No, because the program has a secular purpose and allocates aid based on religiously neutral criteria.
choices.B: No, because the program is religiously neutral and is therefore subject to mere rational basis scrutiny.
choices.C: Yes, because the program has the incidental effect of endorsing religion and is therefore subject to strict scrutiny.
choices.D: Yes, because the program provides direct aid to faith-based elementary schools.

questions.explanation:
First Amendment religious freedoms
Free exercise Prohibits government interference with (or discrimination against) religious beliefs or conduct
Establishment Prohibits government from favoring (or disfavoring) a particular religion or religion generally

The First Amendment establishment clause, which applies to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment, prohibits the government from showing preference for a particular religion (or religion generally) by participating in or aiding religious affairs. However, government financial assistance that is distributed among religious and secular institutions is permissible if that aid is:

  • secular in nature
  • used only for secular purposes and
  • distributed according to religiously neutral criteria.

Here, the county school board is providing direct financial assistance to religious and secular schools by employing teachers to teach English to students whose primary language is not English (secular aid). The teachers are not involved in religious instruction (used only for secular purpose), and teachers are allocated based solely on the number of nonnative English-speakers enrolled at the school (religiously neutral criteria). Therefore, the program likely does not violate the establishment clause.

(Choices B and C) Under the free exercise clause, laws that intentionally target religious conduct are subject to strict scrutiny. In contrast, neutral laws of general applicability that incidentally impact religious conduct are subject to mere rational basis scrutiny. But here, the question asks whether the program violates the establishment clause.

(Choice D) In the past, the government was prohibited from providing direct aid to faith-based elementary and secondary schools. However, this is no longer true. Direct aid to faith-based schools is now permitted when the above criteria are met (as seen here).

📌 Educational Objective

The First Amendment establishment clause generally prohibits the government from aiding religious affairs. However, the government may distribute financial assistance among religious and secular institutions if the aid is (1) secular in nature, (2) used only for secular purposes, and (3) distributed according to religiously neutral criteria.

📚 References
  • Mitchell v. Helms, 530 U.S. 793, 807–14 (2000) (explaining the requirements to distribute aid to a religious school without violating the establishment clause).
questions.zh-question:
一个县学校董事会采纳了一项计划，将聘请教师为母语非英语的小学生教授英语。这些教师将由学校董事会聘用，并分配到县内所有公立和私立学校。县内大多数私立学校都是信仰基础的，因此该计划已采取程序确保教师不参与宗教教学。分配给每所学校的教师人数将完全基于该校招收的母语非英语学生人数。
该计划是否可能违反《第一修正案》的建立条款（establishment clause）？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为该计划具有世俗目的（secular purpose），并且根据宗教中立标准（religiously neutral criteria）分配援助。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为该计划是宗教中立的，因此仅受合理基础审查（rational basis scrutiny）的约束。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该计划具有附带性地认可宗教（incidental effect of endorsing religion）的效果，因此受严格审查（strict scrutiny）的约束。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该计划向信仰基础的小学（faith-based elementary schools）提供直接援助（direct aid）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Constitutional Law: Individual Rights - First Amendment freedoms

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州学校董事会把英语教学经费分给公立和私立学校时，是否因 设立条款（Establishment Clause） 而违法。

三秒认题路径：

州资助 → 私校也收 → 只做世俗 → 中立分配 → 通常合法

核心法律规则

设立条款（Establishment Clause）要求政府不能偏袒某个宗教，也不能用公款去推进宗教活动，但可以把 世俗性质（secular in nature） 的资助发给宗教和世俗机构一起用。关键是三点：只用于世俗目的（used only for secular purposes），而且按 宗教中立标准（religiously neutral criteria） 分配。考场意思：如果老师只教英语、不碰宗教教学，名额又按非英语学生人数来分，这类项目通常过关。

核心判例： Mitchell v. Helms —— 说明对宗教学校的直接资助，只要满足世俗用途、世俗目的和中立分配，通常不违反设立条款。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决吗？
YES如果是终局判决，通常直接进入普通上诉，不用走附带命令。
NO不是终局，就看有没有法定中间上诉；本题没有。
再看附带命令原则三要件：
重要权利
特权问题确实重要。
独立于实体
披露争议和主案可以分开看。
立即上诉
卡死点：终局后仍可救济
结论只要还能在终局后主张排除、撤销或重审，就通常不能立刻上诉。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然私立学校很多是宗教学校，把老师派进去就是政府在帮宗教。

但考试真正问的是：这些钱是不是 世俗资助（secular aid），是不是只做英语教学，分配时是不是按学生人数这种中立标准走。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 英语教学 是世俗用途，而且教师只按非英语学生人数分配，符合宗教中立标准，所以不违反设立条款。

❌ 概念混淆 | 审查标准误判

✕ B: 把 rational basis 搬来，宗教资助看的是设立条款，不是这套审查。

❌ 法律适用 | 严格审查误套

✕ C: 见到宗教背景就想上 strict scrutiny，但这题问的是资助是否偏宗教。

❌ 事实误判 | 直助旧规则误读

✕ D: 以为 direct aid 一定禁，但现在允许给宗教学校，只要用途和分配都中立。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓资助性质，再看用途和分配标准，别被“学校是宗教背景”这层外壳带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：设立条款（Establishment Clause）不怕宗教学校“拿到钱”，怕的是钱被拿去做宗教事；只要是世俗用途、世俗目的、宗教中立分配，通常就能过。

顺手记口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应法定中间上诉例外时才考虑提前上诉。
